entries.title: 1.2 The Grim World
entries.flavour: The world of Heraldry Skirmish is a realm of old faiths, broken kingdoms, hungry roads, and colder bargains. Kings, princes, bishops, and warlords still raise banners over land they can barely hold. They fight over relics, tolls, doctrine, trade roads, salt, iron, and pride. Their victories are measured in burnt farms and new taxes. Their defeats are carried by peasants who never chose a side.

entries.title: 1.3.2 The Six Climates of Ruin
entries.flavour: Beyond the walls, land has become allegiance. Expedition ledgers still say forest, city, cavern, ice, desert, and swamp. Survivors know better. They use older names. The shape of the world is plain enough to anyone who has walked it. The broken mountains run down its spine. The dead empire and its ruined cities sprawl across the eastern heart. The great forest spreads west to the salt-coast, the ice locks the north, the dunes burn in the south beyond the mountain passes, and the swamps drown the south-east where the rivers give out at the sea. The old imperial roads still join all of it, straight and patient, running out from the Ashlands to every climate that survived. A dry label cannot warn a traveller that a road has memory, a court still sits without lungs, or a pool of black water may be listening.
entries.direction: A sweeping panorama from the spine of the broken mountains showing all six climates under one sky: the great forest to the west, the dead imperial city to the east, ice to the north, dunes to the south, drowned fen to the south-east, and dark cavern mouths in the mountains below the viewer; a lone surveyor with a staff in the foreground.

entries.title: The Greenmark
entries.flavour: The Greenmark is the great temperate forest of the surviving world. It is larger than the maps. Roots take a road within a season and make the mile-stones useless. Travellers report trees shifting at the edge of sight, upright hounds between trunks, and grove-circles where moss stays warm after snow. Foresters cut warning signs into bark for those who know how to read them. The most common sign means turn back even if the voice ahead is your own. The forest is no wilderness. It is a country that does not recognize human law.

entries.title: The Ashlands
entries.flavour: The Ashlands are the cities of the old empires after fire, law, and death finished with them. They sprawl across the eastern heart of the world, where the imperial roads still run out to every climate like spokes from a shattered wheel. Forums have collapsed into crypts. Temples lean over plazas filled with soot. Streets run black across districts no living guide will enter twice. Lamps still burn in shrines whose gods have no congregation. Patrols still cross boundaries that vanished before the current Bastions had names. The Ashlands are rich because whole treasuries died under stone. They are feared because the city still knows how to count.

entries.title: The Undermarches
entries.flavour: The Undermarches begin under every place that claims to have a foundation, and run deepest beneath the broken mountains at the world's centre. Mines break into older shafts. Older shafts open into tunnels no pick made. Surveyors return with maps that disagree with themselves. Wells sour overnight. Cellars breathe in winter. Borders on the surface mean little below, where passages run under rivers, burial hills, and walls the Bastions call secure. Down in the true dark the deep elves keep their own houses and their own law, older than any empire and crueller than any court that ever sat above. The deep does not need to invade. The surface keeps falling into it.

entries.title: The Pale City
entries.flavour: In the north, winter has become government. Cities that once held tens of thousands stand ice-locked, their gates frozen mid-closing. Towers crack in the cold. Courts, offices, processions, and taxes continue in forms no living citizen would recognize. Hearthhold sends parties north with oil, fire-charms, and instructions to leave tribute on the old road. No one agrees who first made that bargain. The snow covers ruin with clean hands. It heals nothing.

entries.title: The Sun-Drowned
entries.flavour: South of the broken mountains, the dunes have climbed over the wealthiest realms the world ever boasted of. Tomb-cities of the priest-kings break the horizon like teeth. Salt flats glitter where harbours stood. The desert leaves the dead in sight, enthroned, armoured, embalmed, or half-uncovered by wind. Saltspire's ledgers call the southern routes profitable. Its guides call them damned and charge for the difference. Under the sand, sealed courts keep their lamps lit.

brief.identity: The Sun-Drowned, the southern dunes that have climbed over the richest realms, dotted with tomb-cities, salt flats and unburied dead.
brief.composition: Wide shot across a dune sea toward tomb-cities breaking the horizon like teeth; a half-uncovered enthroned corpse in the foreground, salt flats glittering where a harbour stood.
details: Tomb-city pyramids and spires jutting from the horizon
Salt flat with stranded ship ribs where a harbour once stood
Half-buried throne with an armoured, embalmed corpse sitting upright, wind-scoured
Wind-ripples in dunes drawn as fine parallel lines
A few Saltspire guides and travellers in head-wraps leading pack animals (mules)
Bleached bones and broken statuary
Heat shimmer as sparse vertical lines
activity: Three small travellers trudge along a dune crest with a guide leading
avoid: Not the Cursed Colossus, Sunken Kings tomb or Saltspire bastion
Do not draw glinting colour or sun-disc flares
No camels (not in source) - use mules or nothing
No reanimated dead: they remain objects

entries.title: The Mire
entries.flavour: Where the southern rivers gave out before the sea, the swamps inherited the rest, spreading across the world's south-eastern lowlands. Bogs swallowed roads. Mangroves grew through village roofs. Stilt-houses lean over water that looks shallow until it opens. Reedmarch survives by toll, ferry, leechcraft, and denial. The hag-courts hold the deep fen, and they keep older bargains than any Bastion will admit to honouring. Everyone there knows The Mire is rising. No one profits from saying it aloud. The dead drift below the walkways. Sometimes they drift back.

brief.identity: The Mire, the southeastern swamps where rivers give out, where bogs swallowed roads and the dead drift below the walkways.
brief.composition: Water-level view along a plank walkway through a drowned village; mangroves grow through the roofs of stilt-houses, pale shapes drift beneath the surface.
details: Leaning stilt-houses over dark water
Mangrove roots bursting through a roof
Plank walkway with missing boards
Water that looks shallow but opens in a darker circle
Pale drifting shapes beneath the surface (faces, hands) in fine lines
Reeds, floating weed, hanging moss, a heron-like bird
A lantern on a pole, unlit
activity: A lone toll-ferryman poles a flat boat in the far distance, tiny
avoid: Not Reedmarch itself (no barges, council hall or toll bridges) and not Vossegar's cathedral
No horror close-ups: dead shapes stay ambiguous and faint
No lettering
Not the Blighted Heartwood or Titan fen scenes

entries.title: 1.3.3 The Six Bastions
entries.flavour: Each Bastion is a fortified holding: a walled town, a fortress-chapel, a sealed mining city, a stilt-town behind river-locks. None ruled before the Fall. They survived because they were small enough to be missed, lucky enough to be spared, or stubborn enough to close the gate while neighbours screamed outside. Now they are the great powers of what remains.
entries.direction: A great Bastion gate grinding shut at dusk, guards straining at the windlass inside while desperate figures outside reach for the closing gap.

brief.identity: The six Bastions survived the Fall by closing the gate while neighbours screamed outside.
brief.composition: A great Bastion gate grinding shut at dusk, seen from the outside looking in at a low angle; guards strain at the windlass within while desperate figures reach for the closing gap.
details: Massive double gate of iron-bound timber halfway closed
Gatehouse arch with a portcullis chain, a murder-hole above and a stone relief with no legible text
Windlass with spokes and a drum and chain, guards leaning on it
Pikemen at the gate with faces turned away
Outside crowd of refugees with bundles, a mother holding a child at arm's length through the gap
Wall-top watchers with torches, one lowering a rope
Dust and trampled mud at the threshold
activity: Four guards heave the windlass
Several refugees surge at the gap, reaching hands
A few pikemen hold them back with spear butts
brief.atmosphere: Hard survival bought with others' lives.
avoid: Not a specific Bastion's gate (no Deepwarden great gate, no Greythorn timber)
No monsters at the gate
Do not depict violence against the refugees
Not a postern-gate departure scene

entries.title: Greythorn
entries.flavour: Greythorn is a timber-walled town among ancient oaks at the last surviving crossroads of the western forest road. It endures because it pays the forest. Each autumn, tithe-bundles are left at the standing stones. Each spring, the gate-wardens count the foresters who returned, then count the tools of those who did not.

entries.title: Sablekeep
entries.flavour: Sablekeep is a fortified chapel-town built into the throat of a ruined imperial city, where the Ashlands meet the eastern edge of the forest and the old roads run straight on into the dead empire. It survives by burning. Consecrated braziers stand at every gate, bridge, and chapel window. They are never permitted to go out. The lower terraces rest on the bones of an older temple, and the bones are not all the right shape.

brief.identity: Sablekeep, a fortified chapel-town built into the throat of a ruined imperial city where the Ashlands meet the eastern forest, ruled by the Sable Watch, which survives by burning.
brief.composition: View from the straight imperial road looking up at the chapel-town climbing terraces in the throat of the ruined city; braziers burning at every gate, bridge and chapel window.
details: Terraced chapel-town in dark stone with narrow buttresses and a bell turret
Lower terraces resting on the bones of an older temple, some arches oddly shaped, almost rib-like, but not clearly bones
Consecrated braziers on iron stands at gates, bridges and windows, flames drawn as ink strokes
Ruined imperial city walls and colonnades rising behind
Eastern forest edge pressing on one flank
Gate with a bridge over a dry cut and warrior-priests in dark cloaks on watch
Smoke rising in thin lines
activity: Warrior-priests tend braziers at the gate, small
A column of travellers approaches on the road
brief.atmosphere: Austere, fanatical vigilance against the dead city.
avoid: Not a standard castle; a chapel-town crowded on terraces
Do not show readable emblems of the Watch
No Hearthhold-like central fire or Deepwarden gate
No bones shown explicitly as skeletons

entries.title: Deepwarden
entries.flavour: Deepwarden is a sealed mining city carved into the foothills of the broken mountains. It survived the Fall by closing its great gate. Half the city was on the wrong side when it closed. The half that survived now lives in the upper terraces above what its people call simply the Dark.

brief.identity: Deepwarden, a sealed mining city carved into the foothills of the broken mountains, which survived by closing its great gate and now lives in upper terraces above the Dark.
brief.composition: View from the upper terraces down over the sealed great gate and into a black void below, the Dark; forge smoke rising behind and lantern lights dotted across the terraces.
details: Carved terraces and stairways cut into rock with stone balustrades
The great gate sealed, a vast iron-bound stone door set in a gorge
The Dark below as an abyss of solid black, with a few tiny lantern points
Forge chimneys and smoke columns
Lantern Council members with lanterns of consecrated flame on poles
Mining cranes, tram tracks and ore carts
Dwarven masonry with heavy lintels, no readable text
activity: Small figures with lanterns cross the terraces
A guard watches the sealed gate from a parapet
avoid: Not a forge interior
No visible creatures in the Dark
Not a stone castle on a hill
Do not show the gate open or being closed
must: The gate is closed

entries.title: Hearthhold
entries.flavour: Hearthhold is a walled town in the high north, built around the Great Hearth that has burned without interruption since the Fall. If the Hearth goes out, Hearthhold dies: first the children, then the elderly, then everyone. Every resident takes a turn on the fire-watch. Children are taught to feed the flame before they are taught to read.

brief.identity: Hearthhold, a walled town in the high north built around the Great Hearth that has burned unbroken since the Fall; the smallest, poorest and bravest Bastion.
brief.composition: Interior view across a snowy square toward the Great Hearth, a vast stone fire-pit and chimney with a side-chamber chapel; a ring of walls and training ground behind.
details: Great Hearth: massive stone hearth under a tall chimney, flames drawn in ink
Fire-watchers in furs feeding it with logs and peat
A child handed a log to feed the flame
Side-chamber chapel with a small arched door
Snow-covered roofs, icicles and walls around, wall-top training ground
Stacked fuel, hand-carts and ladders
Banner of the Hearth Marshal without readable device
activity: Fire-watchers tend the Hearth in shifts
Children carry logs
A sentry walks the wall
brief.atmosphere: Fragile warmth against the northern dark.
avoid: Not the Pale City climate view
No glow rays from fire, use ink
Not a luxurious hall; poor and cramped
No lettering

entries.title: Saltspire
entries.flavour: Saltspire is a tower-city built around a deep, sacred well at the centre of an oasis ringed by salt-pans and the bones of older cities. It has the only reliable water for a hundred miles. This makes it wealthy. It also makes it hated.

brief.identity: Saltspire, a tower-city built around a deep sacred well at the centre of an oasis ringed by salt-pans and the bones of older cities; wealthy and hated.
brief.composition: Distant approach across salt-pans toward a cluster of tall towers around the oasis; caravans in the foreground, the sacred well-head at the heart.
details: Slender tower-city of stacked towers with narrow windows around a central well-house
Oasis palms and a green belt around the walls
Salt-pans in geometric basins with raking crusts
Bones of older cities as broken columns on the plain
Mercenary and nomad guards on towers
Water-carrier lines and cistern tops
Caravan of mules and carts at the gate
activity: Caravan approaches the gate
Guards watch from towers
Water-bearers walk in a line
avoid: Not a bare small oasis camp (that is the Oasis Raiders scenario)
No visible dunes monsters
Do not depict the well being sounded
Not Reedmarch or Sablekeep silhouettes

entries.title: Reedmarch
entries.flavour: Reedmarch is a stilt-town raised over log pilings on a network of barges, ferry platforms, and toll bridges. It is the only crossing for 30 miles in any direction. Its people are ferrymen, smugglers, apothecaries, leech-tenders, and corpse-haulers. They know what is buried under their floors. They prefer not to discuss it.

brief.identity: Reedmarch, a stilt-town raised over log pilings on barges, ferry platforms and toll bridges; the only crossing far and wide, populated by ferrymen, smugglers, leech-tenders and corpse-haulers.
brief.composition: Water-level view from a ferry at the toll bridge, looking at the stilt-town with its patchwork of platforms and barges; a barge carrying the Marsh Council hall moored in the middle.
details: Log pilings and plank platforms with huts and ladders
Toll bridges with a rope-and-pulley gate and chain
Barge carrying a hall with a shingled roof (Marsh Council hall)
Corpse-hauler barge with covered bundles
Leech tanks and apothecary stalls on platforms
Reeds, hanging nets and ferry ropes
Smugglers' skiff moored at pilings
activity: Ferrymen pole barges
A corpse-hauler unloads bundles
A toll-keeper counts coin on a bridge
avoid: Not the Mire climate image (a drowned village, no town)
No clear view of what is under the floors
Not a stone town
No lettering

entries.title: 1.3.4 Magic in the Dying Lands
entries.flavour: The Five Traditions all survived the Fall. None survived intact.
entries.direction: A still life on a cracked altar: five damaged implements, one per tradition - a scorched spellbook, a chipped holy symbol, a bloodied ritual knife, a withered antler-and-holly charm, and a cracked crystal - each broken in its own way.

brief.identity: The Five Traditions of magic (Arcane, Divine, Druidic, Sorcery, Psychic) all survived the Fall, none intact.
brief.composition: Still life on a cracked stone altar viewed at slight elevation; five damaged implements arranged in a rough arc, each broken in its own way.
details: Scorched spellbook with a burnt corner and a warped clasp (Arcane)
Chipped holy symbol on a cracked chain (Divine)
Bloodied ritual knife with a notched blade (Sorcery)
Withered antler-and-holly charm on a frayed cord (Druidic)
Cracked crystal with a fracture across its facets (Psychic)
Cracked altar slab with dust, ash and a candle stub
Thin vine and moss creeping at one edge, a spider web in a corner
avoid: No readable runes or glyph text on the book
Do not depict magic effects or glow
Not the Treasure Tables still life (these are tools, not coin)
Do not label which tradition is which

entries.title: 1.3.5 Monstrous Threats
entries.flavour: The Monsters of the Dying Lands are not scattered obstacles. They hold the world now. They keep roads closed, fields empty, shrines silent, and old borders meaningless. A village may vanish because of hunger, tax, fever, or weather. Outside the walls, those causes often have claws, banners, laws, or names.
entries.direction: An abandoned village street: claw-torn doors, an empty well, and a crude monster banner planted where the market cross once stood.

brief.identity: Monsters hold the Dying Lands now; they close roads, empty fields and set up their own banners.
brief.composition: An abandoned village street seen from one end in perspective, the market cross at the centre carrying a crude monster banner.
details: Claw-torn doors hanging from hinges and deep gouges in timber frames
Empty well with a broken windlass and a dropped bucket
Market cross with a crude banner of hide and bones stuck on top
Overgrown cobbles, a cart on its side, scattered pots
Cottages with open shutters and dark windows
A small crow flock on a roof
Totem-like markings of scratches, no letters
avoid: No monsters visible in the frame
No corpses
No readable device on the banner
Not a burnt farmstead of human conflict, and not a scenario battlefield

entries.title: 1.3.6 Adventurers and the Road
entries.flavour: Adventurers exist because the Bastions need work done beyond the reach of soldiers.
entries.direction: A small party walking out of a Bastion's postern gate along a muddy road, past a gibbet and a weathered warning post, toward a dark forest edge.

brief.identity: Adventurers exist because the Bastions need work done beyond the reach of soldiers; a party of four takes contracts through the gate.
brief.composition: A small party of four walks out of a Bastion's postern gate along a muddy road, seen from behind, past a gibbet and a weathered warning post, toward a dark forest edge.
details: Small postern gate in a thick stone or timber wall with a guard looking down from a wall-top
Muddy road with ruts and puddles
Empty gibbet with a cage and chains
Weathered warning post with scratched marks (not letters)
Dark forest edge as dense hatching ahead
Party gear: packs, shields on backs, a spear, a hooded lantern
Dead-leaf and thistle roadside
activity: Four figures walk single file, one glancing back at the gate
A guard watches from the wall
avoid: Not a heroic departure; no banners flying
Not a Bastion portrait and not a mountain-pass vista
No readable text on the post
No monsters in sight

entries.title: 1.3.7 Legends and Echoes
entries.flavour: The Dying Lands remember. They do not remember kindly.
entries.direction: A barrow field at dusk where faint ghostly warriors of an ancient battle re-enact their last charge through the living grass, drawn only in sparse fine lines.

brief.identity: The Dying Lands remember: old battles and legends replay as echoes over the living ground.
brief.composition: A barrow field at dusk with low burial mounds in a wide meadow; faint ghostly warriors of an ancient battle re-enact their last charge through the grass, drawn only in sparse fine lines against solid living landscape.
details: Grassy barrows with a standing stone and an old spear half-leaning
Living grass drawn in firm confident strokes while ghosts use broken thin outlines
Ghost cavalry and foot soldiers with antique helmets and round shields charging left to right
A ghostly banner without device
Dead tree and a crow
Low sun-hazed horizon with sparse horizontal strokes
A lone shepherd or traveller on a rise as the only solid figure
activity: Ghostly warriors charge across the field
A single traveller watches from a barrow, small
avoid: No gradient or glow on the ghosts: line only
No gore, no skeletons
No named legend figures (Saint Cael, Ysolde Vane) depicted
Not the Haunted Mausoleum or crypt interiors

entries.title: Human
entries.flavour: Humans are short-lived strivers who raise fragile things in a brutal world and call the result civilization. They learn fast, adapt faster, and persist in places that wear steadier peoples down to nothing.
entries.direction: A human traveller of a Bastion in layered road clothes with a pack, walking staff and short sword; ordinary, weathered and determined.

brief.identity: A Human adventurer, medium-sized, the plain short-lived 'striver' people who persist where steadier peoples fail, shown as a traveller in a Bastion's service.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view mid-stride on a short patch of rutted track, walking staff planted ahead, head turned back over the shoulder toward unseen pursuit.
details: Layered road clothes: patched tunic, belted over-coat, hooded mantle pushed back
Walking staff of plain ash, scuffed iron ferrule
Short sword in a worn scabbard at the left hip
Travel pack with bedroll and tin cup lashed on
Ordinary unremarkable face, stubble, weathered skin, determined set jaw
Mud-caked boots and frayed hem
No horns, fur, scales or pointed ears: wholly ordinary proportions
brief.atmosphere: Plain weathered resolve, a small life walking through a vast dying land.
avoid: No exotic features: the Human must look unmarked beside the other ancestries
No armour plate or heroic pose: this is a traveller, not a Fighter
Do not copy the Elf's long cloak or the Halfling's hood

entries.title: Halfling
entries.flavour: Halflings keep to hearth smoke and hidden roads, and to the quiet wisdom of staying alive while larger folk blunder into the dark. They are small and quick, and far harder to break than strangers ever expect.
entries.direction: A halfling traveller in a hooded cloak with a sling, a well-kept pack and a cooking pot, alert and capable.

brief.identity: A Halfling adventurer, small-sized, hearth-and-hidden-roads folk who survive by staying unseen, shown as a capable traveller in a Bastion's service.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view, crouched low on one knee, sling hand drawn back, eyes alert and wary.
details: Child-sized body with adult proportions: stocky limbs, broad round face, no beard
Deep hooded cloak with mended hem
Leather sling with a round stone, other stones in a belt pouch
Well-kept pack with a small cooking pot and ladle tied on the outside
Bare, hairy-topped feet or light soft boots
A tuft of weeds and a fist-sized stone at its feet that hint at its small scale
Wary but calm expression
brief.atmosphere: Quiet alertness, hearth-smoke practicality in a hostile place.
avoid: Do not make it a cute child or cartoon: adult, grounded proportions
No pointed ears (that is Elf/Gnome territory)
No wall, building or other figure
No sword: its kit is sling, pack and pot
must: Small, about child height, with adult proportions

entries.title: Dwarf
entries.flavour: Dwarves are cut from sealed stone halls, old grudges, and craft traditions older than most fallen kingdoms. Hardship did not sour them so much as harden them, and little in this world meets one of them head-on and walks away whole.

brief.identity: A Dwarf adventurer, medium-sized but broad and heavy, from sealed stone halls and old craft traditions, shown as a hardened traveller in a Bastion's service.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view, braced wide-stanced, lantern held forward in one hand with a round shield strapped on that forearm, handaxe ready in the other hand.
details: Very broad shoulders, short thick limbs, stocky frame, human-sized but far heavier in build
Long braided beard with metal rings, heavy brow, deep-set eyes used to the dark
Heavy mail or plated chest armour worn with ease, scuffed and re-riveted
Round shield strapped on the lantern arm, handaxe in the other hand
Lantern with a shuttered iron housing
Thick hobnailed boots planted on a small patch of worn flagstone
Stone-cut craftsmanship in belt buckle and axe head
brief.atmosphere: Granite stubbornness, a person built to be struck and remain standing.
avoid: Not a comic dwarf: serious proportions, no oversized hat or cartoon nose
No horned helmet
Do not give it a greataxe (that is the Orc adventurer's kit)
No stair, doorway or other scenery
must: Broad and heavy build: shoulders very wide for the height, thick short limbs, no slender lines

entries.title: Elf
entries.flavour: Elves are shaped by older forests and longer memories, and carry a grace that seems almost inhuman to the hurried peoples of the age. They move lightly, notice much, and bear the weight of beauty and loss without letting it show.
entries.direction: An elf traveller, tall and lean, in a long weathered cloak with a longbow and quiver, calm and watchful.

brief.identity: An Elf adventurer, medium-sized, tall and lean, a graceful, long-memoried traveller in a Bastion's service.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view standing at ease on a patch of leaf litter, longbow lowered in one hand, head tilted as if listening, one hand resting on the quiver.
details: Tall, lean build with long limbs and a long neck
Long pointed ears swept back, high cheekbones, calm eyes that notice much
Long weathered travelling cloak, faded and mended, pinned at one shoulder
A tall longbow nearly the elf's own height, quiver of fletched arrows
Soft boots and bracers; light, unfussy kit
Fine, sparse hair loose or in a narrow braid
Sparse leaf litter at its feet
brief.atmosphere: Elegiac grace, beauty and loss held back behind composure.
avoid: Not a Deep Elf: pale skin and dark armour belong to that entry, here keep light open clothes
Do not pose it drawing the bow: it is at ease
No glowing or magical effects
No heavy armour

entries.title: Gnome
entries.flavour: Gnomes hold that every lock, mechanism, and buried device hides a lesson, and that the lesson is usually worth the risk of learning it. They are clever and precise, drawn to the exact dangers that sensible folk step around.
entries.direction: A gnome traveller with tinkering tools and lenses on a bandolier, a small crossbow and a heavy satchel.

brief.identity: A Gnome adventurer, small-sized, a clever, precise tinkerer drawn to dangerous devices, shown as a traveller in a Bastion's service.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view kneeling over a small trap mechanism lying on the ground, eyepiece lens flipped down, probing it with a thin tool while a small crossbow hangs ready on the back.
details: Child-sized, adult-faced, large nose and one bright eye magnified through a flip-down lens
Bandolier of tinkering tools, picks, lenses and small screwdrivers
Small crossbow slung across the back
Heavy satchel bulging with coils of wire and cogs
Ink-stained leather gloves, apron over practical clothes
Lightly goggled cap or hood, neat tidy clothing
Mechanism with gears showing that it is a trap or lock
brief.atmosphere: Absorbed curiosity, a happy student of lethal things.
avoid: Do not turn it into a steampunk robot or give it huge goggles beyond one lens
Do not duplicate the Halfling's sling and cloak silhouette
Not toy-like: grounded proportions

entries.title: Goblin
entries.flavour: Goblins learn fast hands and quicker feet, and the plain truth that the weak survive by being where the blow is not. They fight mean, flee smart, and take every edge a hard world leaves lying about.
entries.direction: A goblin adventurer in a Bastion's employ: patched but well-kept leathers, a short blade and lantern, wary intelligence in the face; clearly a hired hero, not a raider.

brief.identity: A Goblin adventurer, small-sized, quick of hand and foot, shown as a hired hero in a Bastion's employ (an ally, not a raider).
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view creeping forward, lantern held out and low in one hand, short blade held back ready in the other, poised to dodge.
details: Child-sized body, long pointed ears, large expressive eyes, wide mouth showing a tooth
Patched but carefully kept leather jerkin and trousers
Short blade with a clean bright edge, lantern with a good wick
Bastion livery scrap or a plain tabard end tucked at the belt, no lettering
Alert intelligent face, wary rather than malicious
Belt with pouches and a coil of cord
Bare lean forearms, long clever fingers
brief.atmosphere: Wary intelligence, a survivor who chooses where the blow is not.
avoid: Not the Goblin monster: no notched blade, no sling of river stones, no mob, no crude trophies
No hunched malicious snarl
No rags: clean, repaired clothing

entries.title: Orc
entries.flavour: Orcs are raised where weakness is punished at once and hesitation is never forgotten. Strength, momentum, and raw nerve have carried them this far, and they trust those three further than they trust subtlety.
entries.direction: An orc adventurer in a Bastion's employ: heavy travel-worn armour, a greataxe slung, scarred but composed; a sworn hireling, not a raider.

brief.identity: An Orc adventurer, medium-sized and very powerfully built, shown as a sworn hireling in a Bastion's service (not a raider).
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view standing composed and squared at rest, one hand on the haft of a greataxe slung over the back, gaze steady into the distance.
details: Huge shoulders, thick neck, grey skin scarred in old lines across cheek and forearm
Heavy lower tusks, but a composed controlled expression
Heavy travel-worn armour: studded breastplate, pauldrons, battered vambraces, kept oiled
Greataxe slung across the back, haft visible over the shoulder
Plain Bastion tabard worn over the armour, no lettering
Wide boots, belt with plain pouches
No trophies on display
brief.atmosphere: Disciplined restraint, strength held in check.
avoid: Not the Orc monster: no snarl, no trophies, no cleaver, no shield wall
No ragged furs
Do not put the axe in a swinging pose

entries.title: Ratkin
entries.flavour: Ratkin come up from refuse heaps, tunnel warrens, and plague-alleys where numbers, speed, and hunger settled every argument. They know how to scatter, swarm, and strike where the enemy is already bleeding.
entries.direction: A ratkin adventurer in a hooded cloak and Bastion tabard, satchel of scavenged tools, bright watchful eyes; a hired hero, not a scavenger.

brief.identity: A Ratkin adventurer, small-sized, quick and swarming folk of refuse heaps and warrens, shown as a hired hero in a Bastion's service.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view hunkered low on its haunches, one hand cradling a scavenged tool, head tilted with nose and whiskers working.
details: Child-sized body with a rat-like muzzle, long whiskers, round ears and bright watchful eyes
Long scaly tail curled around the feet
Hooded cloak open over a Bastion tabard with no lettering
Satchel of scavenged tools: pliers, hooks, a small crowbar, rolls of cord
Sharp front teeth showing
Clawed but dextrous hands
Cleaned, mended clothing
avoid: Do not make it a plague-ridden scavenger or a monster Ratkin Warrior or Scavenger
No weapons raised: this is an alert hero, not an attack
Do not draw it as a literal rat: upright, humanoid, clothed

entries.title: Deep Elf
entries.flavour: Deep elves are a crueller branch of the elder blood, raised on night, venom, and treachery taught as a fine art. They are graceful and dangerous, and far more at ease beneath the dark than beneath the sun.
entries.direction: A deep elf adventurer who has come to the surface: pale skin, a hood pulled against daylight, fine dark armour and a curved blade; an outcast hireling, not a warrior of the deep courts.

brief.identity: A Deep Elf adventurer, medium-sized, an outcast of the cruel night-bred branch of the elder blood who has come to the surface as a hireling.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view stepping forward into daylight, one hand raised against the glare under a deep hood, curved blade held low in the other.
details: Pale skin, long pointed ears, slim graceful build, narrow shadowed eyes
Deep hood pulled low against daylight, scarf at the throat
Fine dark armour: close-fitted scale or lamellar with plain trim, no court heraldry
Curved single-edged blade with a plain grip
Long hard shadow cast across the small patch of ground at its feet
Gloved hands, long cloak edge
Controlled, wary expression
brief.atmosphere: Elegant discomfort, a creature of night enduring the sun.
avoid: Not the Deep Elf Warrior or Priest monster: no ornate court armour, no hand crossbow, no quarterstaff
Not a light-cloaked surface Elf: keep dark gear and hood
No spider imagery

entries.title: Demonborn
entries.flavour: Something infernal stains the demonborn line, whether by old pact, curse, or ancestral trespass. Doors do not open for them, but fire parts, fear bends, and darker powers sometimes answer when they are called.
entries.direction: A demonborn traveller with small horns, a tail and ember-like eyes, dressed in a plain pilgrim's cloak.

brief.identity: A Demonborn adventurer, medium-sized, of infernal-stained blood, shown as a plain-cloaked pilgrim traveller in a Bastion's service.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view standing still, one hand half-raised as if about to knock, cloak parted to show a tail, face turned to the viewer.
details: Small curved horns breaking through the hair
Slender barbed tail emerging from under the pilgrim cloak hem
Eyes drawn as dark rings with a tiny white point, unlit and without glow
Plain pilgrim's cloak, rope belt, simple staff or satchel slung
Calm, slightly world-weary face
Warm hands, slightly long dark nails
brief.atmosphere: Quiet apartness, the face of someone doors never open for.
avoid: No bat wings, hooves or fiery body: it is a person with horns and a tail
No fire effects or glow
Do not give it a weapon raised or demonic pose
Not an Imp or Demon monster
No door, house or other scenery

entries.title: Drakeblood
entries.flavour: The drakeblood carry the remnant of an older majesty in the blood, as blessing, burden, or half-remembered debt. The world is fallen, but power still answers them in the old language of flame, storm, and scale.
entries.direction: A drakeblood traveller with scaled skin along jaw and hands and a ridge of small horns, in a heavy cloak with a spear.

brief.identity: A Drakeblood adventurer, medium-sized, carrying the remnant of an older dragon majesty in the blood, shown as a heavily cloaked traveller in a Bastion's service.

entries.title: Courier

entries.title: Performer

entries.flavour: A Fighter is forged in places where hesitation gets people killed.
