No doorway, arch or chapel

entries.title: Wizard
entries.flavour: A Wizard is formed through study that most would not endure. Fragments of knowledge, careful notes, and repeated failure shape their craft. Power is taken apart, understood, and rebuilt with precision.

brief.identity: A Wizard, Caster class: scholar of rebuilt power; packages of Quarterstaff, Magnifying Glass, Torches, Elven Dagger, Sling, Scroll of Arcane Bolt.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view standing, one hand raising a small scroll to a magnifying glass held in the other, staff tucked under the arm.
details: Long layered robe, scuffed hem, ink stains on sleeves
Quarterstaff under the arm
Round magnifying glass with a brass rim
Scroll partly unrolled, filled with abstract scribbles, no letters
Satchel and book strap across the chest
Elven dagger at the belt
Thin face, a short beard or cropped grey hair, squinting
avoid: Not the Sorcerer or Psion: no spell effects or levitation
No pointy star-covered hat
No glowing orbs

entries.title: Psion
entries.flavour: A Psion turns inward until thought itself sharpens into a weapon, paring away everything that does not serve. What others fight to hold steady, a Psion bends to plain intent. The discipline is not so much chosen as survived.

brief.identity: A Psion, Caster class: thought sharpened into a weapon; packages of Dagger, Hide Cuirass, Targe, Throwing Knives, Gambeson, Quarterstaff.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view standing very still with one hand extended, palm out, while three throwing knives hang in the air in front, points turned outward.
details: Three throwing knives suspended in the air at slightly staggered heights
Gambeson or hide cuirass, plain and tight
Dagger sheathed at the belt
Eyes closed or blank white pupils
Hair lifting slightly as in a hush of wind
Gaunt face, taut jaw, veins at the temple
Stillness: no movement lines
avoid: No glowing eyes or auras
Not the Wizard: no staff, no books
Do not draw telekinetic arcs or lines; just suspended knives

entries.title: Trickster
entries.flavour: A Trickster survives by shaping what others take for true. Fact matters less than belief, and belief can be steered. They learn to move freely through the confusion they have already laid down.

brief.identity: A Trickster, Hybrid class: shaper of belief and illusion; packages of Elven Rapier, Shortbow, Elven Dagger, Smokestick, Caltrops, Lockpicks.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view sidestepping a blow with a flourish, rapier flicked out in a feint, trailing cloak flap, smoke curling at the feet.
details: Elven rapier with a swept hilt in a feinting line
Leather coat with ornate stitching and mismatched cuffs
Smokestick burning at the belt, thin wisp rising
Small bag of caltrops at the hip
A faint extra outline (a second, thinner-line copy) of the same figure just beside the shoulder
Sly half-smile, tilted head
Light dancing footwork, one heel lifted
brief.atmosphere: Poised mischief, the moment before everyone looks the wrong way.
avoid: Not the Rogue: no lockpicking, no crouch
Do not draw two solid figures: the double must be a thin broken black outline only
No jester costume or mask

entries.title: Sorcerer
entries.flavour: A Sorcerer is handed power they never asked to carry. It comes fast and demands to be spent, and left to fester it consumes the one who holds it. Spent well, it can settle everything in a single breath.

brief.identity: A Sorcerer, Caster class: carrier of unasked-for power; packages of Quarterstaff, Dagger, Sling, Gambeson, Bandages.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view bracing against its own power, one arm extended with a palm facing the viewer and a small crackling arc of ink-drawn lightning, the other hand clamping the bandaged forearm.
details: Bandaged forearms, old scars and fresh dressings
Hair and cloak flung back by unseen wind
Plain gambeson, torn sleeve
Sling and dagger at belt
Wide eyes with solid-black pupils and a thin white ring
Veins or branching marks on the neck
Lightning rendered as sharp black zigzag strokes, not glow
avoid: Not the Wizard: no scrolls, no magnifier, no staff pose
No glowing aura
No gore

entries.title: Druid
entries.flavour: A Druid knows the world was never owned by those who built upon it. Stone cracks, root spreads, and time takes everything back into the dark soil. A Druid has seen that plainly, and chosen to serve it rather than resist it.

brief.identity: A Druid, Caster class: servant of the world's slow reclamation; packages of Quarterstaff, Club, Wooden Shield, Sling, Elven Sickle, Leather Coat.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view standing barefoot in tall grass, staff planted in one hand and the other palm open and low, a crow perched on the staff head.
details: Leather coat covered in lichen stains and patched with bark-like cloth
Quarterstaff carved with root-like twists
Sprig crown of leaves and a few small twigs in the hair
Sickle at the belt
Bare feet in grass, vines curling round the staff
Weather-lined face, calm eyes
Tall grass around the shins, a few fine rain lines
avoid: Not the Tier 3 tradition image: no bark skin or antlers
No animal companion beyond the crow
No glowing magic

entries.title: 7.6 Treasure Tables
entries.flavour: Treasure in the Dying Lands is never clean. Coin comes from burial hoards, failed relief columns, chapel vaults, drowned roads, damned shrines, dead merchants, broken armies, and rooms sealed by people who feared being found. A purse is often the last record of a life. A crown may have passed through dirt, blood, ash, salt water, and another thief's stomach before it reaches a living hand.
entries.direction: A still life of grim treasure: a rotted purse spilling tarnished coins beside a skeletal hand, a mud-caked crown, a cracked reliquary and a salt-crusted signet ring.

brief.identity: Treasure in the Dying Lands is never clean: coin and relics come from hoards, vaults and the dead.
brief.composition: Still life on a stone slab at slight elevation: a rotted purse spilling tarnished coins beside a skeletal hand, a mud-caked crown, a cracked reliquary and a salt-crusted signet ring.
details: Rotted leather purse with a frayed drawstring spilling coins
Skeletal hand with finger bones curled near the coins
Mud-caked crown with dull gems and a bent circlet
Cracked reliquary box with a missing hinge
Salt-crusted signet ring on a stone
Coins hatched to feel dull, no readable stamps
Cobweb, grave dirt and a spilled bone button
avoid: Not the Magic traditions still life or the melee weapon still life
No readable coin inscriptions
No glinting sparkle effects
No gore

entries.title: 7.8 Melee Weapons
entries.flavour: Many of the arms below carry names from an older, wider world than the Bastions now remember: the long-bladed messer, the notched swordbreaker, the throwing cross, the bladed scourge, the weighted cord, and the hook-and-chain. They reach the Dying Lands as salvage, tribute, and trade goods, carried up the southern routes through Saltspire and bartered onward through Reedmarch. How a blade is named changes nothing about how it cuts. Each is listed here under the name the traders used.
entries.direction: A still life of salvaged arms laid on sacking: a long-bladed messer, a notched swordbreaker, a throwing cross, a bladed scourge, a weighted cord and a hook-and-chain.

brief.identity: Salvaged arms from an older wider world that reach the Dying Lands as trade goods through Saltspire and Reedmarch.
brief.composition: Still life laid out on a sacking cloth viewed from above at an angle: a long-bladed messer, notched swordbreaker, throwing cross, bladed scourge, weighted cord and hook-and-chain, spaced evenly.
details: Langes messer: long single-edged blade with a nagel-style hilt
Swordbreaker with a notched back and a heavy guard
Throwing cross: four-armed bladed star-cross
Bladed scourge: multiple lashes ending in small blades
Weighted cord with a heavy ball at one end, coiled
Hook-and-chain: a long chain ending in a barbed hook
Burlap sack texture, a trader's tag as a blank rectangle, rope bindings
avoid: Not the treasure still life
No weapons beyond the six named, no swords of legend
No readable maker's marks
No gore or blood
must: Only the six named weapons

entries.title: Tier 1 Arcane Spells (d20)
entries.flavour: The first lessons any surviving academy still teaches: force, fire, and the manipulation of what the eye reports. Apprentices roll for what their masters had time to pass on.
entries.direction: A young apprentice at a scarred practice post conjuring a small flame in one hand while a shimmer of force bends the air before the other.

brief.identity: Tier 1 Arcane Spells: the first lessons of any surviving academy (Arcane Bolt, Burning Hands, Ice Ray, Force Push, Phase Step).
brief.composition: A young apprentice in three-quarter view beside a scarred practice post, conjuring a small flame in one palm while a shimmer of force bends the air before the other hand; mid-height. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Apprentice in a plain, too-large robe with chalk and ink stains
Practice post with chopped and scorched marks
Small flame drawn as a single clean ink flame cupped in the palm
Air distortion drawn as bent parallel lines before the other palm
A few cracked flagstones underfoot
Anxious concentrated face, tongue-tip between teeth
A battered wooden staff leaning on the post
avoid: No lettering on tome pages or scrolls: marks only as abstract scribble
Not a grown Wizard: young, small and unsure
No big fireball or lightning
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.3 Arcane Spells, Tier 1

entries.title: Tier 2 Arcane Spells (d20)
entries.flavour: Beyond the apprentice work lie the spells that bent the old empire's wars. Each was copied from a library that has since burned.
entries.direction: A wizard hurriedly copying a spell from a scorched tome by candlelight while the library behind them burns.

brief.identity: Tier 2 Arcane Spells: wartime spells copied from libraries since burned (Fireball, Haste, Blink, Sleep, Dispel).
brief.composition: A wizard seated at a small folding desk, copying from a single scorched, half-burned page onto a fresh sheet; above the fresh sheet the copied spell already stirs as a small sphere of ink flame hovering over the quill; three-quarter view. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Hunched wizard on a camp stool at a folding desk, quill in hand
One scorched loose page with charred edges and unreadable marks, the only remnant of a burned library
A small sphere of flame drawn as clean ink tongues hovering above the fresh sheet
A few sparks drifting up from the sphere as flicked ink flecks
Spilled ink pot and loose pages
A satchel of rescued scraps at the feet
Intent face, deep shadow under the brow
avoid: No lettering on tome pages or scrolls: marks only as abstract scribble
No bookshelves, library hall or burning building
No large explosion: the flame stays small
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.3 Arcane Spells, Tier 2

entries.title: Tier 3 Arcane Spells (d20)
entries.flavour: These are the spells the towers killed to keep. What a wizard recovers at this tier, they recover from ash, ciphers, and the dead.
entries.direction: A wizard sifting ash and cipher-scraps among robed corpses on the floor of a ruined tower, a sealed book clutched to their chest.

brief.identity: Tier 3 Arcane Spells: the spells the towers killed to keep (Meteor Impact, Disintegrate, Time Break, Reality Warp).
brief.composition: A wizard standing amid ash and cipher-scraps on a cracked mosaic floor, a sealed, chained book clutched to their chest while the scraps lift and turn slowly around it, two robed corpses sprawled at their feet; high-angle view. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Standing wizard in tattered robes, one hand holding a sealed book bound with chains and a lock
Two robed corpses sprawled on the fractured mosaic floor
Drifting ash and ink-scrap pieces
Ash scraps lifting and circling the sealed book as if drawn to it
A toppled orrery frame
Wary glance upward
Hard diagonal light in hatch
brief.atmosphere: Grim scavenger's triumph over a tomb of scholars.
avoid: No lettering on tome pages or scrolls: marks only as abstract scribble
No gore or visible wounds on the corpses
Do not make the wizard heroic
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.3 Arcane Spells, Tier 3

entries.title: Tier 1 Divine Prayers (d20)
entries.flavour: The plainest mercies the surviving faiths can still call down: light, mending, and the courage to stand one more round.
entries.direction: A priest raising a lantern whose light falls on a wounded soldier, the wound visibly knitting closed.

brief.identity: Tier 1 Divine Prayers: plain mercies (Sacred Flame, Guiding Light, Healing Touch, Blessing, Sanctuary).
brief.composition: A priest raising a lantern whose light falls on a wounded soldier seated at their feet, the wound visibly knitting closed; mid-shot. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Priest in a plain habit with a hooded head, lantern held high
Soldier seated on the ground, bandaged arm in lantern light
Wound drawn as a long line fading to fine hairlines
Cone of light drawn with sparse straight radiating strokes
A few dust motes as flicked ink flecks
Weary but tender expressions
avoid: No halo or glow wash: light shown only with line and white space
No lettering on the lantern
No visible gore
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.4 Divine Prayers, Tier 1

entries.title: Tier 2 Divine Prayers (d20)
entries.flavour: Prayers answered less often and at greater cost. The gods that remain are listening, but they are tired, and they keep accounts.
entries.direction: A weary cleric kneeling at a cracked roadside shrine beside a ledger of offerings, candles guttering.

brief.identity: Tier 2 Divine Prayers: prayers answered less often and at greater cost (Radiant Burst, Circle of Protection, Guardian Angel, Benediction).
brief.composition: A weary cleric standing at a cracked roadside shrine-stone, tipping coins one by one into an offering dish as a faint circle of protection rises around their feet; low side view. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Standing cleric, hood back, weary face, one hand tipping coins into a dish
Waist-high cracked shrine-stone with a toppled small statue
Open ledger with abstract ruled lines lying on the shrine-stone
Two guttering candles beside the dish
A ring of thin upright ink strokes rising from the ground around the cleric
Satchel and travel-worn boots
Rain streaks beginning
avoid: No lettering on tome pages or scrolls: marks only as abstract scribble
No visible deity or angel
No kneeling figure
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.4 Divine Prayers, Tier 2

entries.title: Tier 3 Divine Prayers (d20)
entries.flavour: At this height a prayer is not asked but demanded, and something always answers. Whether it is the god prayed to is a question the devout do not raise aloud.
entries.direction: A priest with arms raised on a hilltop, demanding, as a vast ambiguous shape takes form in the storm clouds above.

brief.identity: Tier 3 Divine Prayers: prayers demanded rather than asked (Divine Wrath, Heaven's Spear, Resurrection Light, Sunburst).
brief.composition: A priest with arms raised on a bare hilltop, demanding, as a vast ambiguous shape takes form in the storm clouds above; low angle looking up. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Small silhouette on a barren hilltop, robes whipped by wind
Arms thrown wide, head tipped back
Storm clouds drawn as dense swirling crosshatch
A vast, ambiguous form in the clouds: shoulders, perhaps a hand, not a clear face
Beams of sparse straight lines breaking from the cloud
One bare thorn tree on the hilltop
Tiny discarded staff at the priest's feet
avoid: Do not resolve the cloud shape into a clear god or angel
No lettering or symbol
Do not make the priest triumphant
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.4 Divine Prayers, Tier 3

entries.title: Tier 1 Sorceries (d20)
entries.flavour: Sorcery does not study. It bleeds. These first workings cost little blood and never fail, which is how they teach the unwary to want more.
entries.direction: A close view of a sorcerer's cut palm, drops of blood rising and twisting into a small crackling spark.

brief.identity: Tier 1 Sorceries: cheap blood workings that never fail (Chaos Bolt, Bloodspark, Scorch Step, Ember Net).
brief.composition: A close view of a sorcerer's cut palm and forearm, drops of blood rising and twisting into a small crackling spark; the arm thins into white paper at the elbow.
details: Open palm with a shallow cut
Drops of blood rising as small black teardrops
A spark of ink-drawn jagged lines at the apex
Old scars across the wrist and forearm
Thin bandage strip unwound
Plain sleeve rolled to the elbow
avoid: No gore pools; the cut is a single fine line
No glowing wash
Do not show a face fully

entries.title: Tier 2 Sorceries (d20)
entries.flavour: The price climbs with the power. A sorcerer who reaches this tier has already learned what their veins are worth and decided it a fair trade.
entries.direction: A gaunt sorcerer with scar-laddered forearms channelling a crackling storm between their hands.

brief.identity: Tier 2 Sorceries: the price climbs with the power (Volatile Fireball, Chain Shock, Stormskin, Shardstorm).
brief.composition: A gaunt sorcerer with scar-laddered forearms channelling a crackling storm between their hands; three-quarter view, standing braced. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Forearms bare, with ladder-like rows of old scars
Gaunt hollow-cheeked face
Storm drawn as a knot of hard black jagged lightning between the hands
Hair and tattered sleeves flaring outward
Cracked flagstone floor under braced feet
Fresh drops of blood on the wrists
Dark robes in torn layers
avoid: No glow wash
Not a Tier 3 consumed look: body intact
Do not copy Tier 1's palm close-up

entries.title: Tier 3 Sorceries (d20)
entries.flavour: The workings here do not care whether the caster survives them. Sorcerers who command this tier are counted among the things other people pray against.
entries.direction: A sorcerer half-consumed by their own working, a vortex of force tearing up the ground, villagers praying on their knees at a safe distance.

brief.identity: Tier 3 Sorceries: workings that do not care whether the caster survives (Catastrophe Sphere, Gravity Collapse, Ashen Vortex, Meteor Line).
brief.composition: A sorcerer half-consumed by their own working, a vortex of force tearing up the ground around them, two or three villagers praying on their knees, small and faint at a safe distance; the sorcerer centre. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Sorcerer lit from within by white-line cracks across skin, body partly dissolving to ash flecks
Vortex shown as spiral crosshatching tearing a crater
Flying chunks of earth and flagstone
Two or three kneeling villagers, small and faint at the vignette edge
Cloak torn into streamers
Pained, resigned face
avoid: No gore
No fleeing or large villagers: they stay small and praying
No glow wash

entries.title: Tier 1 Druidic Rituals (d20)
entries.flavour: The oldest circles teach these first: the small agreements with root, weather, and beast that the Greenmark still honours.
entries.direction: A druid kneeling with one palm pressed to an exposed root, a hare and a crow watching, rain beginning to fall.

brief.identity: Tier 1 Druidic Rituals: small agreements with root, weather and beast (Thorn Dart, Entangling Roots, Regrowth, Fog Bank).
brief.composition: A druid kneeling with one palm pressed to an exposed root as thin roots curl up around the wrist and a low fog begins to gather, a hare watching; low view at root level. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Kneeling druid in a lichen-stained coat, hood back
Hand flat on a thick twisting root
Hare sitting alert in the foreground
Thin roots curling up from the earth around the wrist
Low fog drawn as sparse horizontal strokes
Damp moss and fern detail
Quarterstaff laid on the ground
avoid: No magical glow
Do not show full transformation
No oversized or magical animals
No crow or other birds
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.6 Druidic Rituals, Tier 1

entries.title: Tier 2 Druidic Rituals (d20)
entries.flavour: Here the rituals stop asking the wild for favours and begin speaking its language. The forest answers in kind, and not always gently.
entries.direction: A druid speaking aloud as the surrounding trees bend toward them and roots heave up out of the earth.

brief.identity: Tier 2 Druidic Rituals: speaking the wild's language (Wall of Vines, Spike Growth, Summon Dire Wolf, Wild Dominion).
brief.composition: A druid speaking aloud as two or three trees at the vignette's edge bend toward them and roots heave up out of the earth; low view with the druid centre. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Druid standing with open mouth, arms spread palm-down
Two or three trees leaning inward with branches reaching like fingers
Roots heaving up from broken ground
Falling leaf scatter and flung soil as flicked ink flecks
Ferns flattening in a ring of wind
Cloak flaring
Staff in one hand
avoid: Do not let the trees have faces
No glowing aura
Do not copy Tier 3's bark-skin
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.6 Druidic Rituals, Tier 2

entries.title: Tier 3 Druidic Rituals (d20)
entries.flavour: At this tier a druid no longer borrows from the living world. They become a clause in its oldest contract, and the world keeps its terms.
entries.direction: A lone druid on a ridge, arms raised, as a colossal storm front drives against a mountain and tears its flank loose in a landslide.

brief.identity: Tier 3 Druidic Rituals: becoming a clause in the oldest contract, with weather as the druid's weapon (Avatar of the Wild, Verdant Dominion, Summon Treant, Maelstrom).
brief.composition: A low wide view up a storm-lashed ridge: a lone druid stands small on a rocky outcrop in the lower left, arms spread, cloak and hair torn sideways by the wind. A colossal storm front, a towering wall of churning cloud with a funnel of wind turning at its heart, rises over the whole upper half of the picture and drives against a great mountain on the right; the mountain's flank is breaking away, a landslide of rock and uprooted pines sliding down. Small vignette, densest at the druid and the storm's heart, thinning into white paper.
details: Small druid in a weathered hooded cloak on a rock outcrop, arms raised and spread, back mostly to the viewer, no face detail needed
Cloak, hair and a staff's trailing cords streaming flat in the wind
Towering storm front drawn as huge rolling cloud masses in bold dark shapes, with rain curtains as long fine diagonal strokes
A tightening funnel of wind and cloud above the mountain, ringed by torn trees and flung debris
Great mountain with a cracking flank: boulders and a slab of rock tumbling, pines uprooted and sliding with the slide
Trees on the ridge bent flat in one direction, a few leaves and branches flying
Lightning as a single jagged branching bolt, drawn as a thin white-and-black fork, never a glow
brief.atmosphere: Awe and dread: nature unleashed and obeying one small figure. Epic scale, with the druid tiny against the weather.
avoid: No hollow, hole or cave in any tree or mountain
Not a Treant monster and no giant tree-person
No glowing eyes, glow, halos or radiating light rays
No lettering or readable runes
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.6 Druidic Rituals, Tier 3 (Maelstrom, Avatar of the Wild)

entries.title: Tier 1 Psychic Abilities (d20)
entries.flavour: The first disciplines of the unquiet mind: to push, to read, to hold a thought steady where the world wants it scattered.
entries.direction: A psion seated with closed eyes, pebbles hovering in a slow ring around them and a candle flame standing perfectly still.

brief.identity: Tier 1 Psychic Abilities: the first disciplines of the unquiet mind (Telekinetic Push, Precognition, Psychic Veil, Mind Link).
brief.composition: A psion seated cross-legged with closed eyes, pebbles hovering in a slow ring around them and a candle flame standing perfectly still; straight-on view, symmetrical. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Seated figure in simple robes with closed eyes
Ring of small pebbles hovering at different heights
Candle with a flame drawn as a perfectly upright narrow tongue
Stone floor with a faint chalk circle
Calm, drawn face
Hands resting open on the knees
avoid: No glowing aura
No lettering in the circle
Not the Psion class pose of hovering knives
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.7 Psychic Abilities, Tier 1

entries.title: Tier 2 Psychic Abilities (d20)
entries.flavour: Deeper into the self than most minds are built to go. Each ability here leaves a mark the psion learns to hide.
entries.direction: A psion alone in a dark corridor, hiding a trembling hand, fine cracks of strain around their eyes.

brief.identity: Tier 2 Psychic Abilities: each ability leaves a mark the psion learns to hide (Psychic Lance, Mind Control, Temporal Skew, Psychic Renewal).
brief.composition: A psion alone, leaning one shoulder on a rough boulder, hiding a trembling hand from which the air ripples faintly, fine cracks of strain around their eyes; mid-shot. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Figure leaning on a rough boulder
One hand clasped in the other to hide a tremor
Hairline cracks radiating from the eyes like fine crazing
Sweat beads and tired face
Faint concentric ripples bending the air around the hidden hand
Collar pulled high
Drip of dark fluid from the nose
brief.atmosphere: Private strain and fear of being seen.
avoid: No glow
No thick or glowing cracks: thin lines only
Do not draw other characters
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.7 Psychic Abilities, Tier 2

entries.title: Tier 3 Psychic Abilities (d20)
entries.flavour: At this tier the boundary between thought and world thins to nothing. What the psion imagines, the battlefield is briefly obliged to believe.
entries.direction: A psion on a battlefield where stone steps and a wall rise from nothing at their gaze, enemies stumbling as the ground obeys the psion's thought.

brief.identity: Tier 3 Psychic Abilities: thought and world merge (Gravity Singularity, Reality Shear, Telekinetic Crush, Mass Domination).
brief.composition: A psion on open ground where stone steps and a wall rise from nothing at their gaze, two or three small enemy soldiers stumbling at the vignette's edge as the ground obeys the psion's thought; psion centre-left. Small vignette, densest at the caster and thinning into white paper.
details: Psion standing still with a locked gaze, hand slightly raised
Rising stone steps and a wall emerging from the ground in stacked blocks
Ground cracks and floating debris fragments
Two or three small enemy soldiers tripping and falling back
Dust drawn as dry-brush drag and a few ink flecks
Tattered coat edges lifting
avoid: No glow or beams
No monsters: the enemies are ordinary soldiers
Do not use the Tier 1 pebble ring
sources: 8. Powers and Traditions: 8.7 Psychic Abilities, Tier 3

entries.title: Giant Tarantula
entries.flavour: A hand-span of bristled legs around a body the size of a war helm, the giant tarantula stalks the Greenmark's leaf litter on stilted, deliberate steps. Their fangs weep a venom that turns a victim's muscles to wet rope. They spin no snares, preferring to run prey down and pin them where they fall. Foragers keep one eye on the canopy, because the largest specimens hunt from above and drop.

brief.identity: Giant Tarantula, Greenmark Skirmisher, small: a hand-span of bristled legs around a body the size of a war helm, a forest-floor venomous hunter.
brief.composition: High three-quarter view from above, looking down on the spider as it stands still on bare packed earth: the body in the centre and all eight legs radiating evenly around it like the spokes of a wheel, four on each side, every leg drawn whole from body to clawed foot and every foot planted on the ground, no leg raised, crossed, overlapping another or hidden by the body; fangs lowered; a discarded war helm lying well apart to one side for scale, touching no leg.
details: Exactly eight legs, jointed and tipped with small claws
Body the size of a war helm, hairy abdomen and cephalothorax
Bristle hairs suggested by short hatch flicks along the contours, not covering every surface
Two large fangs with a bead of venom at the tips
Cluster of eight eyes on a small raised bump
Palps in front of the fangs
Gripping toe-pads suggesting it can climb walls
A rusted iron helm lying apart for scale
brief.atmosphere: Patient, stilted menace in damp leaf litter.
avoid: No web: it spins no snares
Do not make it larger than a dog
No human features
must: Exactly eight legs
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Giant Tarantula [Skirmisher]

entries.title: Goblin
entries.flavour: Knee-high, green-grey, and all elbows and malice, goblins infest the Greenmark's ruined steadings in chittering mobs. Each carries a notched blade and a sling of river stones, and not one will hold a line once the fight turns against them. Singly they are cowards; in numbers they are a tide. Greythorn's gate-wardens read goblin-sign in the chewed bones left along the road.
entries.direction: A Greenmark goblin raider with a notched blade and river-stone sling, part of a mob; hunched and malicious.

brief.identity: Goblin, Greenmark Minion, small: a knee-high green-grey raider of ruined steadings that fights in chittering mobs.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view, hunched and scuttling forward, notched blade out in front, sling and stone pouch at the belt.
details: Knee-high, green-grey (rendered as heavy hatching) wiry body, all elbows and knees
Large pointed ears, long nose, wide mouth full of crooked teeth
Notched, jagged short blade in the right hand
Sling of river stones: leather strap and a bulging pouch of round stones on the belt
Rag loincloth and strips of stolen leather
Malicious narrowed eyes
A few chewed bones on the trampled ground at its feet
avoid: Not the Goblin ancestry hero: no clean kit, no lantern, no tabard
Not the Cave Goblin (blind black eyes) nor Snow Goblin (fur parka)
Do not give a spear (that is the Cave Goblin)
No other goblins or mob silhouettes

entries.title: Beastman
entries.flavour: All fur and grievance, a beastman is a hunched man-shape topped with the head of a goat or boar, their hands ending in black claws. They run the forest edge in warbands, raiding for meat and metal, and there is nothing in them that will parley. They were among the first things the burning years shaped, and they have bred true down every generation since.

brief.identity: Beastman, Greenmark Minion, medium: a hunched man-shape topped with the head of a goat or boar, black claws, a forest-edge warband raider.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view, bent forward and running, both clawed hands spread wide, head low.
details: Goat head with swept-back horns, slotted pupils and a beard
Heavy shaggy fur over a hunched human frame
Black claws on both hands
Goat-like digitigrade lower legs with hooves
Ragged belt of hide strips, no weapon
Torn ear, scarred muzzle, open snarling mouth
Trampled bracken underfoot
brief.atmosphere: Feral grievance, an animal with a grudge.
avoid: No weapons: its attack is Claws
Do not copy the Satyr Reveler (laurel crown, pipes, playful stance)
Do not make it a minotaur

entries.title: Bandit
entries.flavour: Not every threat in the Greenmark has claws. Bandits are deserters, broken tithe-collectors, and folk the Bastions could no longer feed, gathered under whichever of them is cruellest that season. They favour shortbows from cover and blades up close, and they fight dirtiest against anything already down. A full purse or a good pauldron is reason enough.

brief.identity: Bandit, Greenmark Soldier, medium: a deserter or broken tithe-collector turned forest raider, fighting with shortbow from cover and shortsword up close.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view crouched low on one knee, shortbow at half-draw, shortsword laid on the ground within reach.
details: Mismatched scavenged armour: a cracked leather jerkin, one iron pauldron
Shortbow at half-draw with an arrow nocked
Shortsword on the ground beside the knee
Dirty hood and cloth mask pulled below the chin
Hungry, hard face with stubble
Quiver on hip, torn cloak
A few ferns at the knee
avoid: Not the Bandit Captain: no officer's cloak, no heavy crossbow
Not an adventurer class: no clean kit
No cheerful rogue look

entries.title: Satyr Reveler
entries.flavour: Goat-legged and laurel-crowned, the satyr reveler capers at the edge of the firelight, piping on something that was never carved from wood. The music is the weapon: it floods a listener with borrowed terror or walks them gently into the dark. Satyrs were fey once, before the long silence soured them, and their revels end now in shallow graves.

brief.identity: Satyr Reveler, Greenmark Controller, medium: a goat-legged laurel-crowned fey piper whose music floods listeners with terror or lulls them.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view capering on one hoof, pipes at the lips, curved knife thrust in the belt, firelight raking one side.
details: Goat legs with cloven hooves and shaggy thighs
Curled ram-like horns and pointed ears
Laurel crown, withered and brown
Bone-white pipes of many reeds raised to the mouth
Curved knife in a belt sheath
Bare human chest, hollow cheeks, wild grin
Firelight rim on one side; bare trodden earth under the hooves
brief.atmosphere: Sour, soured revelry that is not joyful.
avoid: Not the Beastman: no claws, no hunch, no snarl
Not cute: sour and haggard
No carved-wood pipes
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Satyr Reveler [Controller]

entries.title: Briarling
entries.flavour: A knot of animate thornwood the size of a hound, the briarling scuttles on root-claws with a low, dry rustle, and bursts in a spray of barbed splinters when they are cut down. They cluster in the deep groves the Antlered Warden keeps, spent freely as the forest's first and least-mourned line. Fire is the only sure answer to them.

brief.identity: Briarling, Greenmark Minion, medium-sized: a hound-sized knot of animate thornwood on root-claws, a spent first line of the Antlered Warden's groves.
brief.composition: Low side view of a hound-sized creature, knee-high to a man (a dropped hand-axe lying beside it for scale), scuttling forward on root-claws with its barbed back bristling, head down.
details: Body of twisted tangled wood strands with barbs
Six spindly legs ending in root-claws
Two hollow knotholes where eyes would be, no mouth, no face, no mouth or a split in the bark
Thorn spines in long and short rows along its back
A few withered leaves and moss tufts
Splinters spraying from a cracked limb
Mud and dead leaves under it
avoid: Not a dryad or a treant: no humanoid body, no face
Not a real hound or animal: pure wood
Do not draw flame

entries.title: Dire Wolf
entries.flavour: Bigger than a pony at the shoulder, scarred and yellow-eyed, the dire wolf works the Greenmark in coordinated packs, cutting prey from the herd with grim patience. One is dangerous; a pack is a sentence on any lone traveller. They take the slow, the young, and the foolish, in that order. Greythorn's outriders do not ride alone in wolf season.

brief.identity: Dire Wolf, Greenmark Skirmisher, medium: a pony-sized yellow-eyed pack hunter that cuts prey from the herd.
brief.composition: Low three-quarter view of the wolf stalking forward in a crouch, head lowered, hackles raised.
details: Shoulder as high as a pony, heavy powerful forequarters
Scarred hide with torn ear and a notch in the muzzle
Eyes with pale rings and dark pupils; yellow rendered as pale open ring
Lips curled to show long fangs
Thick ruffled mane and back hackles
Four legs only; thick paws with claws
Leaf litter under the paws
avoid: Do not make it a werewolf (no upright stance)
Do not copy Tundra Wolf (white coat, snow) or Blackfire Hound (flame)
No saddle
No other wolves
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Dire Wolf [Skirmisher]

entries.title: Orc
entries.flavour: Broad as a doorway and armed with battleaxe and shield, the orc is the Greenmark's most disciplined raider, grey-skinned and heavy-jawed, their lower tusks jutting above a wall of shields. Where beastmen break, orcs hold their formation. A warband takes a steading methodically, gate by gate, and savours the hard fight more than the loot it wins.
entries.direction: An orc raider of the Greenmark with crude trophies, a notched battleaxe and a battered round shield, mid-snarl, nothing like a sworn hireling.

brief.identity: Orc, Greenmark Soldier, medium: a broad, disciplined, grey-skinned raider with lower tusks, armed with battleaxe and shield, a warband member that holds formation.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view mid-snarl, advancing with a heavy round shield raised on the forearm and a notched battleaxe raised in the other hand, trophies swinging from the belt.
details: Broad as a doorway, grey skin, heavy jaw, lower tusks jutting upward
One-handed battleaxe with a broad notched blade
Crude trophies: bone strings, a skull and teeth, tied at the belt and shoulder
Layered hide and iron plate scraps; a heavy iron-rimmed round shield on the forearm, battered and dented
Scarred knuckles and brow
Fierce open-mouthed snarl
Trampled earth and ash underfoot
avoid: Not the Orc ancestry hero: no tabard, no composed bearing, no clean armour
Not a Bugbear (shaggy, long-armed)
No greataxe and no sword
must: One-handed battleaxe in one hand, round shield on the other forearm
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Orc [Soldier] (RC488 Battleaxe, Shield Wall)

entries.title: Bugbear
entries.flavour: Seven feet of shaggy, long-armed menace with a flat face and fur the colour of dead bracken, the bugbear moves through the undergrowth in a silence they have no right to. They strike from arm's reach before their quarry knows they are there, rising out of cover with a spiked morningstar already swinging. They much prefer the ambush to the open fight. Where bugbears lair, goblins serve as their terrified scouts.

brief.identity: Bugbear, Greenmark Soldier, medium: a seven-foot, shaggy, long-armed ambusher with a flat face and a spiked morningstar.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view rising out of bracken, long arm drawn back with the spiked morningstar about to swing from arm's reach.
details: A head and more taller than a man, arms reaching to the knees
Shaggy fur the colour of dead bracken, drawn in long hatch lines
Flat face, small eyes, broad nose, wide mouth
Spiked morningstar with a long haft
Leather scraps and a belt of bones
Knee-high bracken parting around its legs
Silent poised stance
avoid: Not an Ogre: lean and long-limbed, not a hulking thing
Not a Beastman: no horns or hooves
Not a Blood Ape: no knuckle-walking

entries.title: Harpy
entries.flavour: Half-mortal and half-carrion-bird, the harpy nests in the Greenmark's broken towers and sings travellers off the road and into their talons. The song is a lure that no resolve fully shakes. Up close they are filth and hooked claws, shrieking as they rake. Their hunger is older than the Fall, and it was never once satisfied.

brief.identity: Harpy, Greenmark Cannon, medium: a carrion-bird monster the size of a man, with a vulture's body and a withered, hag-like head, nesting in broken towers and luring travellers into its talons with its song; it flies.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view swooping down on beating wings, both taloned feet thrust forward, gaunt head jutting forward mid-shriek, over a small patch of bare ground.
details: A vulture's body, covered entirely in filthy, matted feathers from the neck down
A withered, hag-like head with a hooked nose, ragged matted hair and hollow cheeks
Large carrion-bird wings, ragged feathers, long primaries
Two scrawny, sinewy arms below the wings, ending in hooked claws
Legs of a bird of prey with hooked talons
Open mouth mid-shriek, solid black
A scatter of bones on the ground below
avoid: Not a siren or angel: ragged and foul
No wing-arms: the wings and the arms are separate limbs
No bare skin on the body: feathers cover it
must: Clawed hands on the arms; bird talons on the feet
Wings and arms both visible

entries.title: Goblin Shaman
entries.flavour: Hung with fetishes of bone and crow-feather, the goblin shaman is the one goblin their own kind fears more than the enemy. They hang behind the mob and spit hexes that wither courage and rot resolve. Their magic is small and spiteful, scavenged from older powers they do not begin to understand. Kill them, and the warband's nerve tends to break with them.

brief.identity: Goblin Shaman, Greenmark Controller, small: a goblin hung with bone and crow-feather fetishes who hangs behind the mob and spits hexes.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view standing on a low stump, gnarled staff raised in one hand, other hand flinging a spit of dark hex-marks.
details: Knee-high goblin with a larger head and long fingers
Cloak of crow feathers and clinking bones
Gnarled staff topped with a skull and feathers
Necklace of finger bones
Headdress of antlers or bird skull
Hex rendered as short dark dashes from the hand
Bare stump top under its splayed feet
avoid: Not the plain Goblin: no sling
Do not draw glow
No other goblins
must: Small and knee-high, with gnarled staff and fetishes
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Goblin Shaman [Controller]

entries.title: Bandit Captain
entries.flavour: The bandit captain held a real commission once, or says so often enough to be believed. Armoured in looted mail and barking orders a crew will actually follow, they turn a rabble into something that fights like soldiers. They parry the first blow, answer the second, and spend their underlings freely to keep their own skin whole. Greythorn carries a standing bounty on three of them by name.

brief.identity: Bandit Captain, Greenmark Elite, medium: a commissioned-or-claiming leader in looted mail wielding a longsword and a heavy crossbow.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view standing with longsword levelled forward to command, heavy crossbow slung at the hip, cloak hanging from the shoulders.
details: Looted mail hauberk with mismatched officer's pauldron
Longsword with a fine crossguard and a chipped blade
Heavy crossbow slung across the back or hip
Faded officer's sash and scarf
Scarred face, narrow gaze, firm jaw
Boots with spurs, belt of keys
A battered wooden crate at its feet
brief.atmosphere: Hard, practised command: a looted-mail leader who makes a rabble fight like soldiers and spends them to stay whole.
avoid: Not the plain Bandit: higher status, upright, armoured
No ornate royal gear
No horse
No underlings or other figures
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Bandit Captain [Elite]

entries.title: Dire Bear
entries.flavour: The dire bear is the Greenmark grown teeth, a shaggy mountain of muscle that stands twice a man's height and swats deadwood aside to reach whatever they have smelled. They maul with both forepaws and finish with a bite that splits shields. Hunters who corner one rarely walk home. They bear no malice; they are only enormous, and always hungry.

brief.identity: Dire Bear, Greenmark Brute, large: a shaggy mountain of muscle twice a man's height, mauling with forepaws and a shield-splitting bite.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view of the bear reared on its hind legs, forepaws raised and swinging down, jaws open; a small human figure near its feet, drawn small, light and secondary, for scale.
details: Twice a man's height when reared
Huge shaggy hide with matted fur strokes
Broad skull, small eyes, large teeth
Long curved claws on both forepaws
Splintered branches at its feet
Visible shoulder muscle and hump
Broken shield fragment in the dirt
avoid: Not the Gorebeak Bear: no beak or feathers
Not a Werebear
No malice-driven snarl: it is hungry, not evil
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Dire Bear [Brute]

entries.title: Blood Ape
entries.flavour: Slab-shouldered and crimson-furred, the blood ape knuckles through the high canopy and drops onto anything that bleeds. They fight in a building frenzy, both fists hammering faster as their own wounds mount, so the redder they grow the harder they hit. They hold the upper branches of the deep Greenmark and suffer no rival to share them.

brief.identity: Blood Ape, Greenmark Soldier, medium: a slab-shouldered crimson-furred canopy ape that drops onto prey and hammers with both fists.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view of the ape landing from a drop in a crouch on one knuckled fist, other fist cocked back to pummel.
details: Massive shoulders, long arms, short bowed legs
Dense dark fur (rendered with heavy hatching) streaked with red wounds shown as pale gaps
Flat brutal face with heavy brow and fangs
Knuckled fists as big as helmets
Torn twigs scattered on the ground beneath
Wound scars on chest
Leaves falling
avoid: Not a Beastman or Bugbear
No weapons: it uses fists
Do not draw gore
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Blood Ape [Soldier]

entries.title: Gorebeak Bear
entries.flavour: Body of a bear, head and foreclaws of a great owl, the gorebeak is a stitched-together horror of the deep wood, their hooked beak punching clean through plate. They pin prey with raking claws and worry at the gap until something gives. Whether the burning years made these or merely woke them, the foresters cannot agree. The argument is no comfort to the pinned.

brief.identity: Gorebeak Bear, Greenmark Brute, large: a stitched-looking horror with a bear's body and a great owl's head and foreclaws, with a plate-punching hooked beak.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view of the creature charging low, head thrust forward, hooked beak open, foreclaws raking out; a small human figure near its forefoot, drawn small, light and secondary, for scale.

Great owl's head with a facial disk, round eyes and a hooked beak
Foreclaws of an owl: long curved talons
Feathered neck ruff blending to fur
Plate-pierced hook beak with a shred of armour
Four limbs only; no wings
Torn earth flung from its feet
avoid: No wings: it does not fly
Not the Dire Bear: no reared pose, no bear head
Not an owlbear cartoon
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Gorebeak Bear [Brute]

entries.title: Ogre
entries.flavour: Twice a man's height and slope-shouldered, an ogre is a slab of grey muscle and gut bound in stitched hides. They claim a ford or a narrow run between the trees and take a toll of all that try to pass. They do not count coin. They count the heavy, bright things their last few meals were carrying, and swing a tree-trunk club to collect more.

brief.identity: Ogre, Greenmark Brute, large: a twice-man-height, slope-shouldered grey slab of muscle in stitched hides, claiming a ford with a tree-trunk great club.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view standing calf-deep in a small patch of ford water, great club resting on the shoulder, one hand held out for a toll; a small human figure at the water's edge, drawn small, light and secondary, for scale.

Grey skin, bald head, small eyes, underbite
Stitched hide clothes patched with cord
Great club made from a tree trunk with roots at the head
Heavy bright objects (a dented helm and cups) hung from its belt
Stream water around its shins
Open outstretched empty palm
avoid: Not a troll: no claws or regeneration
Not a Forest Troll's lanky build
Not a Gloom Hulk

entries.title: Dryad Grovewarden
entries.flavour: Bark-skinned and crowned in living branches, a dryad grovewarden is the will of an old tree given a shape that can walk and a grudge they can hold. They step between trunks as though they were doorways and bind intruders in grasping root. The Antlered Warden's tithe keeps most groves quiet. Where it goes unpaid, the grovewardens stir.

brief.identity: Dryad Grovewarden, Greenmark Controller, medium: a bark-skinned fey tree-spirit crowned in living branches that binds intruders with roots.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view striding forward, staff extended, roots snaking from its feet into the ground.
details: Bark-textured skin on a tall, slender figure clothed from neck to knee in overlapping leaves and bark plates
Crown of living branches and leaves
Long hair of vines
Entangling staff of twisted wood

Curls of shed bark at its feet
avoid: Not the Briarling: this is a humanoid
Not a Treant: only a person-sized figure
No nudity
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Dryad Grovewarden [Controller]

entries.title: Forest Troll
entries.flavour: Gangling, moss-slick, and stinking of the bog-edge, the forest troll is all reaching arms and a mouth of broken tusks. Their wounds knit shut before the blood has dried, and only fire or acid puts one down to stay. They are stupid, relentless, and forever hungry. Greythorn's woodcutters carry oil for exactly one reason.

brief.identity: Forest Troll, Greenmark Brute, large: a gangling moss-slick bog-edge brute with reaching arms and broken tusks whose wounds knit shut.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view of the troll lurching forward with both long arms reaching, mouth agape; a small human figure near its feet, drawn small, light and secondary, for scale.

Moss patches clinging to slick skin
Broken tusks in a wide mouth
Rending claws on both hands
Old wounds drawn closing as raised stitch-like seams

Not the Swamp Troll (different habitat, mire details)
No fire or oil shown
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Forest Troll [Brute]

entries.title: Werewolf
entries.flavour: A haunted villager by day, a hunched grey killer at the turning of need, the werewolf carries an old curse in their blood. Mundane steel slides from their hide; only silver and magic bite true. They strike from the treeline and are gone before the screaming stops, then circle back for the wounded. Every bitten survivor is tomorrow's werewolf.

brief.identity: Werewolf, Greenmark Elite, medium: a haunted villager's cursed form, a hunched grey wolf-man killer that strikes from the treeline.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view of the beast striding upright, claws spread, torn villager's shirt still hanging.
details: Upright hunched wolf-man with a lupine head and long muzzle
Shaggy grey fur rendered with long hatch
Long rending claws
Torn villager's clothes: shirt strips and a broken belt
Savage open jaws with a long tongue
Digitigrade legs
Moonlight raking one side in sparse lines
avoid: Not the Dire Wolf: this walks upright
Do not show wounds
Not the Werebear or Wererat

entries.title: Green Dragon
entries.flavour: Apex predator of the Greenmark and its oldest liar, the green dragon is a serpentine tyrant the colour of deep moss, spine-crested, their breath a rolling, corrosive poison. They do not rampage; they manipulate, ruling a swathe of forest through fear and bargain. Lesser things bring them tribute in exchange for being spared a while longer.
entries.direction: A typical adult green dragon of its kind, alone, coiled on a mossy rock; no lair, no tribute.

brief.identity: Green Dragon, Greenmark Elite, huge: a moss-coloured serpentine spine-crested tyrant with a corrosive breath; it flies. Typical adult, alone.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view of the dragon coiled on a mossy rock with its long neck raised and head turned toward the viewer, wings folded; a tiny human figure beside the rock, drawn small, light and secondary, for scale.

Spine crest running from the head down the back
Four legs and a pair of folded wings
Horned head with narrow eyes
Moss-textured scales drawn as fine overlapping arcs
Long forked tongue or a slight wisp of breath shown with a few broken strokes
Mossy boulder and bare ground with no treasure
avoid: No lair, no hoard and no tribute
Not a Frost Wyvern (two legs)
Not the Black, Blue or White Dragon: moss/serpentine silhouette with a long neck
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Greenmark Bestiary: Green Dragon [Elite]

entries.title: Undead Warrior
entries.flavour: The Ashlands never disbanded its legions; it merely let them die unburied. An undead warrior is a skeleton or half-rotted corpse in the rusted kit of the old empire, still holding the post they were set to generations back. They fight in ragged ranks, shield to shield, mindless but drilled by sheer habit. There are always more of them in the ash.
entries.direction: A half-rotted corpse, not a bare skeleton, in rusted imperial legion kit with a short sword and a rectangular shield, ash underfoot.

brief.identity: Undead Warrior, Ashlands Minion, medium: a half-rotted corpse in rusted old-empire kit holding its post in the ash.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view of the corpse standing at its post, rectangular shield forward and short sword at the ready, ash drifting at its feet.

Rusted imperial legion kit: segmental armour, plain helm
Rectangular shield, scarred and dented
Notched short sword
Dead hollow eye sockets as solid black
Tattered cloak edge, ash underfoot
avoid: Not bare bones: that is the Skeleton Warrior
Not frosty: that is the Frozen Skeleton
Not ornate: that is the White Court Guard
No other undead in a rank
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Ashlands Bestiary: Undead Warrior [Minion]

entries.title: Undead Crossbowman
entries.flavour: Behind the shambling battle-line stand the crossbowmen, dead marksmen cranking warped windlasses with fleshless fingers. They loose in volleys at whatever their soldiers have fixed in place, and their bolts seek the gaps in armour with horrible patience. They do not tire, flinch, or lose their nerve. Only their bolts run out, eventually.

brief.identity: Undead Crossbowman, Ashlands Cannon, medium: a dead marksman cranking a warped windlass with fleshless fingers in the rear of a battle-line.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view of the figure with a boot in the stirrup, cranking the windlass, crossbow aimed at an unseen mark.
details: Fleshless skeletal fingers on the windlass handle
Crossbow with a warped stock and iron prod
Quilted gambeson rotting to threads and kettle hat
Quiver of bolts at the hip, a few bolts left
Gaunt skull face with hollow sockets
Ash and rubble around the feet

Not a Skeleton Archer: crossbow, not bow
Not a Forsaken Archer: tattered common kit
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Ashlands Bestiary: Undead Crossbowman [Cannon]

entries.title: Ghoul
entries.flavour: Grey, gaunt, and hook-clawed, a ghoul is what hunger makes of a corpse that would not lie still. They lope in packs through the Ashlands' tombs, and their bite carries a paralytic rot that stiffens the limbs. Ghouls take the living and the freshly dead alike, and they are clever enough to cut off the straggler. They were people once, before the long famine that came after the cities burned.

brief.identity: Ghoul, Ashlands Minion, medium: a grey, gaunt, hook-clawed corpse-eater with a paralytic bite that hunts tombs in packs.
brief.composition: Low three-quarter view of the ghoul loping forward on two legs and one knuckled hand, head forward, jaws opened.

Long hook claws on each finger

Sunken eyes, thin lipless face
Tattered burial scraps
Bony hunched posture

Not the Frost Ghoul: no ice or frost
No weapons

entries.title: Possessed Corpse
entries.flavour: Not all the Ashlands' dead rose by design. A possessed corpse is a body worn by something that crept in from the dark between worlds, lurching on borrowed legs toward a wrong, jerking purpose. Their grip does not tire, and they burst in a reek of corruption when they finally fall. Whatever rides them does not speak. They only reach.

brief.identity: Possessed Corpse, Ashlands Minion, medium: a body worn by something from the dark between worlds, lurching toward a jerking purpose.
brief.composition: Full figure in three-quarter view lurching forward with arms outstretched, head lolling to one side.
details: Body in a tattered shroud or peasant clothes
Head tilted at a wrong angle
Mouth stretched open as a solid black void
Dark vapour strands leaking from eyes and mouth
Arms stiff and reaching, fingers curled
Bare feet dragging in ash
Gaping cuts without gore, grey skin
avoid: Not a Zombie of the Mire: no water, no bog plants
Not a Ghoul: stiff, lurching, not feral
No weapon
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Ashlands Bestiary: Possessed Corpse [Minion]

entries.title: Ember Skull
entries.flavour: A single charred head wreathed in green flame, the ember skull drifts the ruins on a cold updraft of malice, lighting the dark with their own hateful glow. They spit gouts of fire at the living from beyond their reach. Old grimoires name them the failed apprentices of the empire's pyromancers, kept burning by their final spite. Snuff the flame and the skull drops inert.

brief.identity: Ember Skull, Ashlands Cannon, small: a single charred head wreathed in flame that drifts on cold updrafts; it flies.
brief.composition: Three-quarter view of the skull drifting in the air above a small heap of rubble, jaw open, a thin fire ray spitting from the mouth.
details: A single charred skull, no body
Tall wavy flame tongues around it rendered as hatched flame shapes
Jaw hinged open with cracked teeth
Eye sockets solid black with small white points
Ray of fire shown as a narrow tapered line
A little rubble below catching sparse cast light
Soot flecks
brief.atmosphere: Small, spiteful ember in the cold.
avoid: No body or wings (it flies without wings)
Not glow: draw flames in line
Do not make it cute
sources: 9.7 The Bestiary, Ashlands Bestiary: Ember Skull [Cannon]

entries.title: Wererat
entries.flavour: Where the Ashlands meet the old sewers and undercrofts, the wererat thrives, a hunched, plague-grey shapeshifter scurrying between man and rat-thing. They bite, then skitter back into the dark, leaving filth-fever in every wound. Mundane blades barely mark them. One wererat is a nuisance; a nest of them is an outbreak.

brief.identity: Wererat, Ashlands Skirmisher, small: a hunched plague-grey shapeshifter between man and rat that bites and skitters back into the dark.
brief.composition: Low three-quarter view of the wererat caught mid-pounce, jaws wide, clawed hand with the rusted blade trailing behind.
details: Hunched half-man half-rat form
Long snout with chisel teeth, whiskers, naked tail
Plague-grey patchy fur and bare skin
Rusted blade gripped in a clawed hand
Ragged clothes of sewer rags
A wet patch of undercroft flagstone under its feet
Small, about the size of a crouching child
avoid: Not the Ratkin ancestry hero
Not the Ratkin Scavenger or Warrior
Do not draw it as a real rat only

entries.title: Spectre
entries.flavour: Grief and rage with the body burned away, a spectre drifts the Ashlands trailing the manner of their death. They pass through wall and armour alike, and their touch drinks the warmth and the years out of the living. Steel finds nothing to bite; only magic answers. The ruined city is thick with them, each one a question that was never answered.

brief.identity: Spectre, Ashlands Controller, medium: grief and rage without a body, a flying incorporeal dead thing that drinks warmth and years by touch.

entries.title: Undead Sentinel
entries.flavour: They guarded the empire's gates in life and they guard the rubble of them in death, tall dead men in iron helm and reach-halberd. A sentinel plants themselves in a breach and will not be shifted, lending their iron stillness to the lesser dead around them. They do not pursue. They only hold, forever, a line that fell centuries ago.
entries.direction: A towering gaunt dead soldier planted in a broken gateway, rusted tower-shield grounded and reach-halberd raised.

brief.identity: Undead Sentinel, Ashlands Soldier, medium: a tall, gaunt dead gate-guard in iron helm with a reach-halberd, who holds a breach forever.

entries.title: Undead Champion
entries.flavour: Raised from the largest corpses the Ashlands could muster, the undead champion is a slab of dead muscle swinging a maul of fused bone. Each blow lands with siege-engine weight and rattles whatever stands beside the thing they struck. They are slow, single-minded, and almost impossible to put off their feet. Where they walk, the lesser dead come on in their wake.

brief.identity: Undead Champion, Ashlands Soldier, medium: a slab of dead muscle raised from the largest corpses, swinging a two-handed war maul of fused bone.

entries.title: Gargoyle
entries.flavour: By daylight a gargoyle is nothing but one more of the empire's stone guardians, perched and patient on a broken cornice. Let prey stray beneath, and the stone splits into claws and a biting maw. Their hide turns aside all but the heaviest blow. The Ashlands bristle with statues, and not every statue is one.

brief.identity: Gargoyle, Ashlands Skirmisher, medium: a stone guardian that looks like statuary until prey strays beneath it; it flies.

entries.title: Stone Sentinel
entries.flavour: A faceless construct of the old empire, the stone sentinel grinds forward on legs of carved granite and hews with a greatsword of carved stone. They feel nothing and fear nothing, and they stop only when they are shattered. The empire raised thousands to guard halls that no longer stand. They guard them still.

entries.title: Minotaur
entries.flavour: Bull-headed and giant, the minotaur stalks the Ashlands' labyrinthine ruins and never once loses their way among the fallen streets. They charge head-down to gore and trample, then wade in with a greataxe. Their senses cut clean through smoke and shadow, so no ambush takes them in their own maze. Old maps mark their haunts with a single horned skull.

entries.title: Night Hag
entries.flavour: A withered crone of the between-places, the night hag slips into the waking world to feed on fear and curse the sleeping. Their claws leave a wound that festers, and when a fight turns against them they step half into the ether and are gone. They bargain, they lie, and they curse the young from the shadows. The Ashlands' long nights are their hunting ground.

entries.title: Forsaken Archer
entries.flavour: The Forsaken were the empire's finest, sworn to an oath that outlived the flesh that swore it. A forsaken archer draws a cursed longbow with a dead marksman's precision, and their arrows leave a clinging curse where they strike. Smoke and shadow do not trouble their aim. They serve Captain Veyr still, exactly as they once swore they would.

brief.identity: Forsaken Archer, Ashlands Cannon, medium: an oath-bound dead marksman of the empire's finest, drawing a cursed longbow.

entries.title: Forsaken Knight
entries.flavour: Dead chivalry in spectral plate, the forsaken knight advances through the ash with a flamberge wreathed in grave-light. They parry with a lifetime's drill written into bone and cannot be slowed or turned aside. Bound by an oath they can no longer recall, they follow Veyr's banner into every fight. Their honour has curdled into compulsion.

entries.title: Forsaken Duelist
entries.flavour: Faster than a dead thing has any right to be, the forsaken duelist fights with a single flashing rapier and a fencer's lethal economy. They wait for a blade to commit, slip the strike, and answer through the opening. In life they were the empire's finest fencer; in death they are the same, only tireless. Veyr keeps the duelists close, for they punish every misjudged swing.

entries.title: Basilisk
entries.flavour: Heavy and eight-legged, the basilisk drags themselves through the Ashlands' rubble behind a gaze that turns flesh slowly to stone. Meet their eyes and the stiffening starts, the limbs first, then the rest. Even their blood petrifies whatever it touches. The ruins are dotted with their leavings, statues of the surprised, caught mid-stride.

entries.title: Ashen Revenant
entries.flavour: An ashen revenant is a corpse-warrior in fire-blackened plate, risen with one purpose welded into their bones: to kill the thing that killed them. They hunt that grudge across the Ashlands with tireless focus, and struck down they claw upright again to land a final blow. Cross their path and you become the grudge. They do not stop until you do.

brief.identity: Ashen Revenant, Ashlands Elite, medium: a corpse-warrior in fire-blackened plate driven by one grudge, clawing upright after being struck down.

entries.title: Iron Golem
entries.flavour: The empire's master-smiths forged iron golems to outlast the dynasty, and in that one task they grimly succeeded. A towering automaton of riveted black iron, they shrug off sword and spear alike and answer with piledriver fists. Edged steel skids from their plates. They guard a throne whose claimant is centuries of dust.

entries.title: Lich
entries.flavour: A lich is an archmage who refused death and paid for the refusal in everything that made them human. A desiccated sorcerer-king in mouldering finery, they command the Ashlands' dead with a gesture and loose blasts of soul-rending necrosis. Destroy the body and they re-form, so long as the hidden phylactery endures. The empire fell. Its worst survivor did not.

entries.title: Kobold
entries.flavour: Knee-high reptilian scavengers with dull scales and dingy picks, kobolds are the Undermarches' scuttling vermin-folk. One alone is nothing; a chittering mob of them, dragging traps and loosing slings from the dark, is a real danger. They know every tunnel and trust not one. Where a single kobold shows themselves, a whole warren is watching.

entries.title: Cave Goblin
entries.flavour: Paler and blinder than their forest cousins, cave goblins have gone so long without sun that their eyes are wide black pools. They jab with jagged spears and bolt at the first hint of a losing fight. They infest the upper deep in nervous packs. A cave goblin's first instinct is to flee toward more cave goblins.

entries.title: Giant Bat
entries.flavour: Leathery-winged and wider than a man is tall, the giant bat navigates the lightless depths by shrieks no living ear can catch. They harry intruders in swooping passes, biting and wheeling away before the answer lands. Torchlight only draws more of them. Whole colonies hang in the upper caverns, and they wake all at once.

entries.title: Vaultfang
entries.flavour: A vaultfang clings to the cavern roof as a flawless imitation of a stalactite, a mottled cone of stone-hard chitin, and they wait. When something passes beneath, they drop, driving their single barbed point clean through helm and skull. They are a living spear that falls exactly once. Few who survive a low ceiling here ever walk easy under one again.

entries.title: Giant Centipede
entries.flavour: Many-segmented and as long as a spear, the giant centipede pours over cave walls on a hundred legs, mandibles dripping a venom that locks the muscles solid. They hunt by vibration in the lightless dark. A bite swells black within minutes. Their shed husks carpet the floors of the oldest tunnels.

entries.title: Noxcloth
entries.flavour: The noxcloth hangs from the cavern roof like a fold of black leather the size of a flung cloak, no different from shadow until they drop to smother. They wrap a victim's head and crush, sightless but needing no eyes in the dark they bring with them. Of all the things that wait on the deep's ceilings, they are the one to fear most.

entries.title: Troglodyte
entries.flavour: Grey, crested, and degenerate, troglodytes are reptilian cave-dwellers whose skin shifts colour to vanish against bare stone. They reek so violently that the stench alone sickens the unready. They hunt in clutches, claws first, fading in and out of the rock. Their territory announces itself by smell long before anything is seen.

entries.title: Giant Black Widow
entries.flavour: Glossy-black and the size of a war-hound, the giant black widow squats in a cathedral of their own webbing, the telltale crimson mark on their swollen back. They fling strands to snare prey from across a chamber, then close to deliver a venom that stops the heart cold. They are the Broodmother's lesser daughters, and they spin the most lethal traps below.

entries.title: Gloomspore Jelly
entries.flavour: A translucent grey ooze the size of a man, the gloomspore jelly creeps over every surface and dissolves whatever they touch. They feel neither pain nor fear. Destroyed at last, they burst in a cloud of soporific spores. They leave the tunnels behind them scoured clean and faintly glistening.

entries.title: Troglodyte Shaman
entries.flavour: The troglodyte shaman daubs themselves in glowing fungus and mutters to things that dwell below even the deep. They call up reeking clouds and spiteful hexes to soften prey for the clutch. Their magic is primitive but real, and older than any empire that ever named it. The other troglodytes give way before them, and so should anything wise.

entries.title: Vault Ooze
entries.flavour: Near-invisible and wall to wall, a vault ooze is a cube of acidic slime that fills a corridor and sweeps it clean of everything that ever breathed. The unwary walk straight in and are engulfed, dissolving while still aware of it. They move in eerie silence, betrayed only by a faint shimmer. The neatest tombs in the deep were swept out by these.

entries.title: Vrymk
entries.flavour: A writhing tangle of stone-grey tentacles around a cruel hooked beak, no broader than a crouching man, the vrymk clings to cavern walls until prey wanders close. Camouflaged against the rock, they lash out with rubbery arms and haul the catch to their maw. They hunt by patience and ambush rather than speed. Anyone who hears a wet, slithering rasp from a bare wall has already been seen.

entries.title: Deep Elf Warrior
entries.flavour: The deep elves quit the surface ages before the Fall and have curdled, in the dark, into something coldly beautiful and merciless. A deep elf warrior fights with poisoned hand-crossbow and finesse blade, seeing perfectly in a lightlessness that blinds everything else. They raid the upper deep for slaves and for sport. Mercy was a surface weakness they bred out long ago.
entries.direction: A deep elf warrior of the deep courts in full dark ceremonial armour with a crescent glaive, in the Undermarches gloom.

brief.identity: Deep Elf Warrior, Undermarches Skirmisher, medium: a coldly beautiful, merciless deep elf raider who fights with a poisoned hand crossbow and a finesse shortsword and sees perfectly in the dark.

entries.title: Deep Elf Priest
entries.flavour: Robed in black silk and bone fetishes, a deep elf priest serves the spider-gods of the deep. They wreathe their enemies in conjured darkness and bend their wills with a single spoken command. From the shadow they have made, quarterstaff in hand, they drive the warriors forward. Their faith is cruelty refined into ritual.
entries.direction: A deep elf priest in layered dark vestments raising a shadow-wreathed sigil staff.

brief.identity: Deep Elf Priest, Undermarches Controller, medium: a black-silk-robed priest of the deep spider-gods who weaves darkness, bends wills with a spoken command and drives warriors on, armed with a plain quarterstaff.

entries.title: Gloom Hulk
entries.flavour: Beetle-backed and the size of a bull, the gloom hulk is a digger armed with great scything claws and four eyes that scramble the mind of anything that meets them. They burrow through solid rock to erupt beneath their prey. Their gaze leaves victims reeling and helpless where they stand. More than one collapsed gallery in the deep is their doing.

brief.identity: Gloom Hulk, Undermarches Brute, large: a bull-sized, beetle-backed digger with great scything claws and four eyes that scramble the mind.

entries.title: Cryptstrangler
entries.flavour: A cryptstrangler passes for a stalagmite taller than a man until their strands uncoil, a stony predator that flings sticky tendrils across a chamber, reels in the catch, and bites them through. They can sit motionless for years between meals. The tendrils come from angles no one expects, faster than anything that still should move. Not every silent column down here is only stone.

entries.title: Elder Vrymk
entries.flavour: Where lesser vrymk lurk as ambushers, the eldest of a brood swells to monstrous size. They are a knot of stone-grey tentacles thick as a man's leg, gathered around a beak that shears clean through plate. They no longer hunt alone; the smaller kin gather to their silent direction and drag prey within their reach. A tunnel scoured of every other living thing is their larder.

entries.title: Evil Eye
entries.flavour: A floating orb of leathery flesh ruled by one great central eye and crowned with writhing eyestalks, the evil eye spits a different doom from each lesser eye. They drift the deep wrapped in an aura that unmakes magic outright. No two of their glares do the same thing twice. They regard every other living thing as a competitor to be erased.

entries.title: Burrowmaw
entries.flavour: An armour-plated horror the size of a wagon, the burrowmaw has a blunt head and a maw that splits their whole face open. They swim through solid stone and erupt beneath their prey in a shower of rubble. They sense footfalls through the rock and leap the last span with their jaws spread wide. The stone trembles faintly before they surface, and that is the only warning anyone gets.

entries.title: Thought-Eater
entries.flavour: A robed, four-tentacled humanoid with an octopus's head, the thought-eater wears grey, slick skin and white, pupilless eyes. They feed on living minds, and a single psychic blast drops a whole party to their knees. They can seize a victim's will and turn them on their own friends. They scheme in the dark beneath the dark, and to meet one is to feel them already reading you.

entries.title: Frozen Skeleton
entries.flavour: Rimed in blue frost, a sword welded to their hand by ice, a frozen skeleton is one of the Pale City's countless dead, still standing the post they were given. They guard avenues that have not seen a living census in centuries. The cold preserves them whole; they will hold that post when the last warm thing in the world goes out. There are always more under the snow.
entries.direction: A frost-rimed skeleton with icicles hanging from its ribs and a sword frozen to its hand, snow drifted around its feet.

entries.title: Snow Goblin
entries.flavour: Gaunt and white-furred, snow goblins den in the Pale City's drifts and tunnels, ambushing out of the whiteout with frost-edged knives. They are invisible against the snow until the moment they move. Cowardly and quick, they strip the frozen dead and bolt from any honest fight. The blizzard hides both their approach and their retreat.

brief.identity: Snow Goblin, Pale City Minion, small: a gaunt white-furred goblin that ambushes out of the whiteout with frost-edged knives.

entries.title: Ratkin Scavenger
entries.flavour: The ratkin are a verminous rat-folk that boiled up into the Pale City when the long winter first came down. The scavengers are their lowest caste, scrawny twitching things in matted grey fur, darting through the ruins to strip anything not frozen to the ground. They swarm, they scurry, and they rarely stand to fight. Where the scavengers pick, the warren is never far behind.

entries.title: Tundra Wolf
entries.flavour: White-coated and built for the killing cold, the tundra wolf pads across ice that would betray a heavier foot. They run in packs that herd prey into the open, where the wind does half the killing. Their bite carries the chill of the Pale City itself. Travellers who hear no howling are in the gravest danger of all.

entries.title: Ratkin Warrior
entries.flavour: A hunched, spear-wielding rat-man in scavenged scraps of plate, the ratkin warrior fights shoulder to shoulder behind a bristling wall of points. Alone they falter; in a shield-rank they hold. The warren feeds them forward in chittering blocks. They die easily and breed faster than they die.

entries.title: White Court Guard
entries.flavour: The White Court is the Pale City's undead nobility, and the guard is its rank and file: a frost-armoured corpse bearing longsword and shield, moving with the cold discipline of a court that never once adjourned. They lock shields across the frozen avenues and advance by the old drill. Death only made them more obedient.

entries.title: Ratkin Seer
entries.flavour: Draped in icicle-charms and half-mad, the ratkin seer spits frost-hexes that sap the warmth and the will from their enemies. They hang behind the warriors, croaking prophecy and curse in the same breath. Their magic is scavenged and unreliable, but a hex that lands at the wrong moment still kills. The warren treats their ravings as law.

entries.title: Frost Ghoul
entries.flavour: A ghoul frozen and reborn in the Pale City's cold, their claws sheathed in killing frost and their hunger undimmed, the frost ghoul hunts in packs through the snow-choked streets. They drag down the living to feed. The cold that should still them only whets their appetite. They do not slow, and they do not stop while anything warm remains.

entries.title: White Court Archer
entries.flavour: From the frozen balconies of the dead city, white court archers loose volleys of ice-fletched arrows, dead marksmen whose aim outlasted the flesh that learned it. They mass their fire on whatever the soldiers have pinned. The cold steadies their hands more surely than any living discipline could. Their quivers never empty.

entries.title: Blackfire Hound
entries.flavour: Cold black flame guttering along their spine, the blackfire hound is a charred beast-shape that leaves a trail of smouldering ash across the snow. Their bite burns with a fire no ordinary frost-ward will stop. They course in packs through the Pale City's ruins, herding prey onto their own burning trails. The snow hisses where they pass.

entries.title: Ice Wraith
entries.flavour: A knife of frozen malice given a drifting, translucent shape, the ice wraith is the spirit of someone who froze to death in the Pale City and never forgave it. Their touch saps warmth and thickens the blood to sludge. Steel passes clean through; only magic bites. They haunt the coldest avenues, hungry for the heat of anything still living.

entries.title: White Court Sentinel
entries.flavour: A greatshield-bearing corpse-knight, the white court sentinel is the dead nobility's bodyguard, planting themselves before their lords and refusing to give ground. They lend their frozen resolve to the soldiers around them and weather blows that would shatter a lesser guardian. They will not pursue and will not break. They only endure, as the court endures.

entries.title: Ice Elemental
entries.flavour: A lurching figure of living glacier, jagged and groaning, the ice elemental freezes the ground they cross and the limbs they land upon. Their slamming fists lock muscle solid in an instant. Fire is their bane; frost means nothing to them. The Pale City's deep cold breeds them where the ice grows thick enough to dream.
