entries.title: Fallen Paladin
entries.flavour: Holy oath turned to grave-frost, the fallen paladin is an undead knight in defiled plate, radiating an aura that withers the courage of all who come near. Their flamberge carries a necrotic chill, and despair leaks off them the way cold leaks off ice. They guard the Pale City's blackest chapels. Whatever vow they broke in life, they keep a darker one now.

entries.title: Werebear
entries.flavour: In the Pale City's frozen wilds prowls the werebear, a hulking man-beast of white fur and ruinous strength, damned kin to the werewolf but built to maul rather than skirmish. They strike with both paws and a bone-cracking bite, and hurl grown men aside. Mundane weapons barely part their hide. A single one can break a war-band.

entries.title: White Court Executioner
entries.flavour: The white court executioner carries out sentences the living court passed centuries ago, a towering headsman whose frost-rimed axe seeks the weakest throat on the field. They stride past the hale to reach the wounded and end them with grim efficiency. The court's justice did not die with the court. It only grew patient.

entries.title: Frost Wyvern
entries.flavour: A lesser cousin of the great dragons, the frost wyvern is a winged reptile the colour of dirty ice, a venom-and-frost sting whipping at the end of their tail. They stoop from the white sky to harry and poison, then climb out of reach before the answer comes. They are cunning rather than wise. The Pale City's frozen peaks are crowded with their roosts.
entries.direction: A frost wyvern on the wing, two-legged and lean, distinctly smaller and rangier than a dragon.

entries.title: Gelid Fiend
entries.flavour: The Pale City's frozen law keeps advocates that were never born under any sun. A gelid fiend is summoned and bound into the cold, a towering devil of blue-white ice and cruel geometry, their hide a lattice of frozen carapace. They raise walls of ice to pen their quarry and enforce judgements no mortal court would dare to sign. They do not tire, bargain, or relent, and the cold around them is the cold of a sentence already handed down.

entries.title: Frost Giant
entries.flavour: Blue-skinned and towering over humans, orcs, and ogres alike, the frost giant goes armoured in glacier-ice and brings a greataxe down like an avalanche. They hurl boulders to scatter foes before they close the distance. The Pale City's oldest streets were built to their scale, by something, for reasons no one living recalls. They rule the high drifts as a king.

entries.title: White Dragon
entries.flavour: The Pale City's frozen sovereign, the white dragon is a feral, ice-crusted wyrm whose breath flash-freezes whatever it touches. Less cunning than their kin but no less lethal, they are pure predatory cold given wings and an appetite. They nest in the highest spire and suffer the White Court about them as courtiers. When they descend, the city's eternal winter only deepens.
entries.direction: A typical adult white dragon, alone on a jagged ice outcrop with wings half-raised; no spire, no city.

entries.title: Fire Beetle
entries.flavour: Hard-shelled and the size of a dog, the fire beetle carries a ruddy inner heat that lights the tomb-passages they infest. They snap with burning mandibles and burst into a gout of flame when crushed. Tomb-robbers prize their glands for their steady light. The beetles prize the tomb-robbers for their meat.

entries.title: Imp
entries.flavour: Knee-high and bat-winged, a barbed venomous tail lashing behind them, the imp flits about the Sun-Drowned tombs as the spiteful servant of darker things. They dart in to sting and wheel away cackling, untroubled by the desert's heat or their own infernal fire. Alone they are more nuisance than threat. They are also a herald of worse to come.

brief.identity: Imp, Sun-Drowned Skirmisher, small: a knee-high bat-winged spiteful fiend with a barbed venomous tail that flits about tombs; it flies.

entries.title: Skeleton Warrior
entries.flavour: A skeleton warrior stands at the post they were set in the year of their death, a sun-bleached frame in the corroded bronze of a priest-king's guard. They still hold the weapon they carried in life, waiting on an order that has not come in centuries. When intruders breach the sealed courts the order arrives at last, and the bones remember their drill. There are always more, ranked in the dark behind them.
entries.direction: A bare sun-bleached skeleton in corroded bronze scale and a crested bronze helm, holding a curved bronze blade, sand underfoot.

entries.title: Corpsehound
entries.flavour: Jackal-headed and quick, the corpsehound runs the dunes between man and beast, hunting the Sun-Drowned's caravans in loping packs. They strike hardest off a running start, scimitar in one hand and slavering jaws beneath. They serve the tomb-courts as scouts and trackers. By the time the laughter reaches you, the pack already has your scent.

entries.title: Gnoll
entries.flavour: Hyena-headed, rangy, and ruled by a bottomless hunger, gnolls sweep out of the Sun-Drowned wastes to fall on anything weaker than themselves. A gnoll that drops a victim grows frenzied and surges straight on to the next. They take slaves and meat and leave the bones in the sand. Their cackling carries for miles in the dry air.

entries.title: Giant Scorpion
entries.flavour: The size of a man and banded in chitin plate, the giant scorpion bears two crushing pincers and a venom-dripping sting arched above their back. They lie half-buried in the dunes and lunge at whatever walks past. Their venom liquefies a body from within. The Sun-Drowned's sands hide thousands of them, each one waiting on a footfall.

entries.title: Skeleton Archer
entries.flavour: The archers of the priest-king tombs stand in alcoves carved to fit them, bows still strung after centuries. The arrows have not rotted; some things are kept by intention, others by spite. They loose in disciplined volleys at whatever the skeleton warriors have engaged. Their aim is exactly as good as it was the day they died.

entries.title: Mummy
entries.flavour: A priest-king's preserved corpse risen in wrath, the mummy comes bound in resin-soaked wrappings and trailing the dread of a dead god's authority. Their touch lays a withering curse, and the mere sight of them can root a victim in terror. Fire is their one true fear. They guard a tomb whose treasures they will not share, not even now.

entries.title: Skeletal Beast
entries.flavour: The bound remains of some great desert predator, the skeletal beast is a charging framework of fang and claw with nothing left in them to slow them down. They run prey to ground across the open sand and tear with bony jaws. No flesh means no fatigue and no fear. The tomb-courts loose them like hounds.

entries.title: Wind Elemental
entries.flavour: A howling spiral of desert air turned malevolent, the wind elemental is a near-invisible vortex that flings sand and bodies with equal ease. They buffet foes off their feet and are barely troubled by ordinary weapons. They haunt the open wastes where the Sun-Drowned's storms are born. You hear them long before the sand begins to bite.

entries.title: Desert Naga
entries.flavour: A great serpent with an almost-human face and the patient cunning of something very old, the desert naga coils among the tomb-pillars. They spit venom from a distance and crush what comes close, hexing the strong into an unnatural sleep. The priest-kings kept them as guardians and oracles. They guard still. They no longer answer.

entries.title: Fire Elemental
entries.flavour: A roaring man-shape of living flame, white-hot at the core and shedding embers at the edges, the fire elemental sets alight everything they touch and scorches whatever strikes them. Water and ice are their only checks; the desert sun is their cradle. They draw a trail of cinders across the tomb-floors. To lay hands on them is to burn.

entries.title: Giant Skeleton
entries.flavour: A looming framework of fused bone twice a man's height, the giant skeleton is what remains of something that was never entirely natural and is far less so now. They move with grinding deliberation, sweeping aside anything in their path with fists like falling masonry. Tomb-city carvings show their kind kneeling before the priest-kings; none show them standing. Whatever they were raised to guard, they guard it still.

entries.title: Medusa
entries.flavour: A serpent-haired figure whose gaze turns the living slowly to stone, the medusa lurks among the statues that were once their admirers. They fight with blade and venomous snake-hair, but their eyes are what fill the tomb-galleries with permanent witnesses. The priest-kings cursed their kind, or rewarded them; the tales cannot agree. Their victims cannot say.

entries.title: Tomb Necromancer
entries.flavour: The necromancers of the Sun-Drowned were the tombs' original administrators, robed officials who chose preservation over death and never gave up their posts. A tomb necromancer is a withered figure in the faded regalia of a dead bureaucracy, raising the buried to enforce statutes no living court remembers. They wither the living with a gesture and call up the dead to fill the gaps in their ranks. Everything they administer belongs to a world that ended.

entries.title: Tomb Guardian

They plant themselves at a threshold and cannot be hurried or frightened. They have held one doorway for a thousand years. They will hold it for a thousand more.

entries.title: Brass Golem
entries.flavour: A burnished automaton glowing with the trapped heat of the forge-rites that made them, the brass golem hammers with fists that sear on contact. Fire cannot harm them; they are fire's own child. The Sun-Drowned's wealthiest tombs are sealed behind these. They do not rust, tire, or reason.

entries.title: Manticore
entries.flavour: A monstrous fusion of lion's body, bat's wings, and a man's leering face, the manticore flicks volleys of iron spikes from their lashing tail. They wait where the dune-road narrows and rain barbs on whatever they have trapped. They savour a meal that begged first. The Sun-Drowned's loneliest trails are their larder.

entries.title: Demon

They hew with a hooked glaive and loose surges of fire that pay no heed to armour. Those near them feel their courage drain away. Something summoned them once, and that something is almost certainly dead by now.

entries.title: Blue Dragon
entries.flavour: The Sun-Drowned's apex tyrant, the blue dragon is a horned, sand-scaled wyrm that burrows beneath the dunes and erupts amid their prey in a lance of lightning. Vain and territorial, they rule a swathe of desert and the tomb-courts caught within it. They hoard beneath the sand and surface only to feed or to punish. The static before their breath raises every hair on the body.

entries.title: Bogling
entries.flavour: Squat and frog-mouthed, boglings lurk chest-deep in The Mire's reeking shallows with spears at the ready. They croak warnings across the water and hurl mud-darts before they close. Cowardly alone, they mass in the hundreds in the deep fens. The Mire's first warning is always the same: a sudden, total silence of frogs.

entries.title: Swamp Goblin
entries.flavour: Slime-streaked cousins of their forest kin, swamp goblins paddle The Mire's channels and blow poisoned darts from the reeds. They melt into the cover and strike from wherever the water hides them. A nuisance one at a time, a hazard in a swarm. They strip the drowned for trinkets and teeth.

entries.title: Zombie
entries.flavour: A waterlogged corpse that The Mire would not keep, the zombie lurches upright in tattered remains, driven by a single-minded hunger. They are slow and mindless and horribly hard to put down, shrugging off blows that would fell a living man. They drift beneath the walkways until something warm passes overhead. Then they reach up.

brief.identity: Zombie, Mire Minion, medium: a waterlogged corpse the Mire would not keep, lurching upright in tattered remains and reaching up from beneath walkways.

entries.title: Stirge
entries.flavour: A bloated mosquito-thing the size of a cat, the stirge carries a needle proboscis and a belly that swells red with stolen blood. They dart in, latch on, and drain until they are pried loose. The Mire's dusk air hums with them. One is an itch; a swarm is exsanguination.

entries.title: Will-o'-Wisp
entries.flavour: A drifting orb of pale corpse-light, the will-o'-wisp lures travellers off the safe paths and into the sucking mire to drown. They hang motionless as a false beacon until prey strays near, then strike with a shock of cold lightning. They feed on the terror of the dying. The kindest-looking light in the mire is the one most likely to kill.

entries.title: Lizardfolk Warrior
entries.flavour: Scaled and cold-eyed, the lizardfolk warrior hunts The Mire as easily in the water as on the rotting banks, fighting with heavy club and javelin in disciplined packs. They are not cruel, only pragmatic; to them the living are meat and territory. They defend their breeding-pools without mercy. The mire is theirs, and they forget no intruder who enters it.

brief.identity: Lizardfolk Warrior, Mire Soldier, medium: a scaled cold-eyed pack fighter with heavy club and javelin who defends its breeding-pools.

entries.title: Lizardfolk Hunter
entries.flavour: A barbed harpoon in their claws, the lizardfolk hunter stalks The Mire's margins, dragging prey off the walkways and into the water where every advantage is their own. They strike from cover and the reeds, unseen until the line snaps taut. Patient and silent, they wait out the careless. By the time they move, you are already in the water.

entries.title: Crocodile
entries.flavour: Grown to monstrous length in The Mire, the crocodile is a log-still ambusher that explodes from the murk to clamp on and drag their victim under in a death-roll. They can lie motionless for hours with only their eyes above the water. The deep channels belong to these. The walkways exist because of them.

entries.title: Lizardfolk Shaman
entries.flavour: Cloaked in dried reeds, the lizardfolk shaman speaks for the swamp-spirits, mending their packmates' wounds and hexing their prey. They hang back among the warriors, croaking invocations over the water. Their magic is old and patient and bound to the mire itself. Kill the shaman and the pack fights harder, but it bleeds out faster.

entries.title: Miasma Serpent
entries.flavour: A bloated water-snake, the miasma serpent exhales clouds of poison gas as they swim, leaving a drifting green pall across the channels. Their bite carries a venom that festers fast. They hunt by lying in the haze of their own making. The mire's foulest-smelling stretches are where they nest.

entries.title: Swamp Naga
entries.flavour: A great serpent with a hooded, watchful face, the swamp naga coils among the drowned ruins, spitting venom and binding prey in their crushing length. They hex the strong to sap their strength before they strike. Older than the mire's human settlements, they remember when the ground was dry. They guard sunken treasures no one else can reach.

entries.title: Giant Constrictor
entries.flavour: Long enough to bridge a channel, the giant constrictor drops from overhanging branches to coil and crush. They strike, immobilize, and squeeze the breath from their prey in the space of a few seconds. Then they slide back into the water before any rescue can reach them. The low branches over the mire are never safe to walk beneath.

entries.title: Shambling Mound
entries.flavour: A heaving mass of animate rot and creeper-vine, roughly man-shaped and utterly tireless, the shambling mound engulfs their prey in their sodden bulk. Lightning only feeds them; blades vanish into the muck. They drift the deep fen absorbing whatever they smother. The mire grows them wherever enough has drowned and rotted together.

entries.title: Swamp Hag
entries.flavour: A warty, weed-haired crone, the swamp hag poles their way through The Mire cursing all they meet, slipping half into the spirit-world when cornered. Their stench chokes out hope. They bargain, they lie, and they feed on misery. The loneliest hut in the mire is theirs, and it is never empty for long.

entries.title: Banshee
entries.flavour: The shrieking spirit of a woman drowned in grief, the banshee is a translucent horror whose wail stops hearts and freezes the blood. They drift The Mire's fog, and their keening carries the plain certainty of death. Steel passes through them; only magic answers. To hear the wail clearly is to be the one they have chosen.

entries.title: Swamp Troll
entries.flavour: A slime-green giant of reaching arms and a tusked maw, the swamp troll hauls themselves through The Mire on all fours, regenerating any wound that fire or acid has not seared. They stink of the bog and hit like a falling tree. They are too stupid to fear and too durable to ignore. Mire-folk keep oil and flint within reach at all times.

entries.title: Hydra
entries.flavour: A many-headed reptilian horror, the hydra wallows in The Mire's deepest pools, each serpentine neck striking on its own and snapping at anything in reach. They cannot be frightened, and they bite back the instant something draws near. Cut a head away and they simply work with the others. They are the apex even the crocodiles fear.

entries.title: Blackwater Wight
entries.flavour: The drowned dead given malice, the blackwater wight is a barnacled corpse-warrior that rises from the mire's black pools, hauling the recently dead up behind them. Their blade drinks the life from those it cuts, and the wound will not fully close until the adventure ends. They command the drowned the way a sergeant commands recruits. The mire's deepest channels are their barracks.

entries.title: Mire Titan
entries.flavour: A colossal amphibian-horror, the mire titan is a froglike bulk of warty hide and lashing tentacles crowned by a vast, distensible maw. They seize prey in their arms and swallow them whole, dissolving them in their acid gut while they still struggle. They are The Mire's living sinkhole. Whole expeditions have gone into one and left only ripples.
entries.direction: A typical Mire Titan alone, waist-deep in fen water, reeds and mud sliding from its body; no geodes or hunters.

entries.title: Black Dragon
entries.flavour: The Mire's sovereign, the black dragon is a sleek, horned wyrm the colour of stagnant water, their breath a hiss of acid. Cruel and patient, they lair in a flooded ruin and rule the fen through terror, taking tribute and tearing apart any who refuse to pay. They swim as easily as they fly. When the frogs go silent and the water stills, they are already close.

entries.title: The Ancient Void Dragon
entries.flavour: Older than the Fall and perhaps its cause, the Ancient Void Dragon is a wound in the shape of a wyrm, their scales drinking the light from the air around them. Their breath neither burns nor freezes but unmakes, peeling away substance until nothing is left. Stars seem to dim where they pass. The wise do not speak their name, and the dead do not speak at all.

entries.title: The Hollow Crown of the Ashlands
entries.flavour: The empire's last emperor died without an heir, and the crown itself took up the rule. A circlet of black iron hovering above an empty regent's robe, the Hollow Crown commands the Ashlands' legions with a dead sovereign's absolute authority. They pass judgement that withers the living and raise the fallen to enforce it. Their throne room is the whole of the ruined empire.

entries.title: The Last Colossus
entries.flavour: A walking fortress of riveted black iron three times a man's height, the Last Colossus groans at every joint with the thunder bound inside them. When the empire knew it was dying, it poured the last of its wealth into one war-construct meant to outlast everything. For centuries they have marched the same patrol, defending an empire that no longer exists. Nothing has yet proven able to stop them.

entries.title: Avatar of the Old Growth
entries.flavour: A towering shape of ancient trunk and grasping root, bark-skinned and crowned with a tangle of antlered branches, the Avatar of the Old Growth is the will of the deep forest given a body to act through. They call the lesser green things to their side and drown intruders in living wood. To kill them is to wound the Greenmark itself. The Greenmark does not forgive.

entries.title: The Broodmother Prime
entries.flavour: In the deepest dark of the Undermarches squats the mother of every giant spider that plagues the deep, a bloated horror the size of a cottage, egg-sacs trailing from them that twitch with the unborn. They flood the field with their brood and bind the survivors in webs for later. Their venom stops a heart in a single beat. The deep, in the end, is their nursery.

entries.title: Captain Veyr of the Forsaken
entries.flavour: Veyr was the empire's greatest captain, who swore their company would never break and held them to it past death itself. Now they lead the Forsaken in spectral plate, a duelist whose paired blades have not slowed in three centuries. They rally their dead soldiers with a voice like a closing tomb. They no longer recall the war they are still fighting. Only the oath.

entries.title: The Frost Bailiff Magistrate
entries.flavour: The Pale City's court needed an enforcer for the sentences its living judges feared to sign, and so it raised one of its own into something colder still. The Frost Bailiff Magistrate drifts the frozen avenues passing final judgement, freezing the guilty where they stand and calling the White Court to carry out the verdict. Their rulings cannot be appealed. Their sentences are always death.

entries.title: The Sun-Crowned Prince
entries.flavour: The greatest of the priest-kings refused to let their reign end and bound their soul into a crown of beaten gold. A wrapped and withered corpse robed in funeral linen, the crown still bright above a face of leather and bone, the Sun-Crowned Prince rules their sealed tomb-court as they ruled in life. They raise their skeletal subjects and scour trespassers with decrees of searing flame. They still believe the world answers to them, and within their tomb it does.

entries.title: The Antlered Warden of the Tithe
entries.flavour: The antlered figure admitted to Greythorn's west gate each winter does not come to bargain when the tithe goes unpaid. They come to collect. A towering shape of bone-antler and living wood, they drag the indebted into their reach and call the wild court to witness. The forest has never broken the agreement, and it does not forgive those who do.

entries.title: The Voice Beneath the Bells
entries.flavour: Survivors describe a small figure at the edge of the torchlight, singing in a tongue that sounds like an old lullaby heard through water. Then the torch goes out. The Voice Beneath the Bells is grief given a child's shape and a drowned chapel's patience, and their song hollows out everyone who hears it. The bells they wait beneath have not rung in a very long time.

entries.title: Maelthorn the Verdant
entries.flavour: Maelthorn is a vast wyrm the deep green of stagnant pondwater, their overlapping scales furred with moss and creeping lichen. They do not hunt, because the Greenmark hunts on their behalf, and Greythorn sends the autumn tithe in place of a war party. Their breath is a rolling fog of poison that wilts all it touches. When they finally stir, the lesser beasts of the wood flee the grove ahead of them.

entries.title: Sirrach the Black
entries.flavour: Sirrach is the Undermarches' buried king, a black wyrm that swims through solid stone and surfaces only to feed. Their breath withers flesh and shortens lives, leaving even survivors diminished. They hoard in galleries no surface-dweller has ever mapped. The stone shudders before them the way a hand shudders before opening bad news.
entries.direction: Sirrach erupting out of solid stone in an unmapped gallery, the rock rippling like water around its black body.

entries.title: Visath the White
entries.flavour: Visath is the Pale City's eternal winter wearing the body of a wyrm, a glacier with wings and a will. Their breath does not merely freeze; it stops time in the flesh, leaving victims locked mid-scream in the ice. They rule from the highest spire and suffer no warmth anywhere in their domain. Where they fly, the snow falls harder, as though the sky itself bows.

entries.title: Khorrun the Dracolich
entries.flavour: Khorrun has not drawn breath since the Fall, yet still they coil atop their hoard in the sealed tomb-galleries beneath the Sun-Drowned. Their bones hold the shape of greed, draped in the tatters of scale and the cold blue fire of undeath, and ledgers stacked to the vault ceiling record exactly who has taken what. They rouse only to punish a debt or devour a trespasser. The lightning that pours from their jaws is the same colour as the witchfire in their empty sockets.

entries.title: Vossegar of the Flooded Cathedral
entries.flavour: Vossegar lairs in a drowned cathedral at The Mire's heart, a sleek black wyrm coiled among submerged altars. Their acid breath strips flesh from bone, and at their will the waters rise to swallow the ground their enemies stand on. They take tribute from every settlement in the mire and devour those who come up short. The bells of their cathedral toll underwater, and the frogs have not sung there in living memory.

entries.title: Scenario 1: Hunt the Wild Beast
entries.flavour: Something out of the deep wood has taken Greythorn's logging camps for their hunting ground, and with them the timber the Bastion is built on. The first deaths were blamed on dire wolves. The next were found driven through splintered palisade timbers, which dire wolves do not manage. Their pelt, skull, and teeth would buy a season behind the walls, and the Council of Captains will pay either way to have the camps cutting again. Comfort and timber have sent both parties into the trees.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Whispering Grove
entries.flavour: The grove is older than Greythorn and older than the western forest road that skirts it. The standing stones hum when no wind passes, and pale lights move between them on moonless nights. Greythorn's farmers leave bread there and do not look back. Scholars call it a site of power. The Council of Captains calls it part of the tithe, and pays it without complaint.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Bandit's Toll
entries.flavour: The western forest road carries Deepwarden iron, Reedmarch salt, and grain between the Bastions, and it is the one artery Greythorn cannot do without. A toll crew has claimed a bend of the trail and nailed its prices to the trees in stolen blood. Caravans wait behind palisades while bread grows dear inside Greythorn's walls. The Council of Captains has stamped a bounty and sent it out with anyone hungry enough to answer.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Spider's Silk Route
entries.flavour: Silk-traders whisper of a ravine in the deep Greenmark where the webs hold steel like thread and fetch absurd prices in Bastion markets. The spinners are the Broodmother's daughters, strayed up from the dark, and the place is on no honest map. That has not stopped a Greythorn merchant from selling the same path through the thorns to two parties at once.

entries.title: Scenario 5: The Ambushed Emissary
entries.flavour: An emissary vanished on the western forest road carrying documents sealed under two rival Bastion laws. One patron in Greythorn wants the courier found breathing. Another, further off, wants the satchel and does not ask after the courier. The deep wood has kept worse secrets, and the Hollow Quarter is not telling.

entries.title: Scenario 6: Ritual of the Old Growth
entries.flavour: An Old Growth elder works slowly over a sickness in the roots, and a Heartwood Totem worth more than most villages stands at the heart of the rite. Greythorn's tithe forbids touching it, and the Council of Captains keeps the tithe because the alternative is the wild court at the gate. Another Bastion, with no forest to answer to, calls the same act salvage. The roots are listening to both.

entries.title: Scenario 1: The Fallen Observatory
entries.flavour: A star-engine once crowned these ruins, and its broken brass arms still turn when moonlight enters the cracked dome. Wizards would give a finger for the instruments scattered across the shifting floors, which is precisely why the Sable Watch wants them carried to Sablekeep and locked away from unregistered hands. The old servants of the place still know the penalty for touching them. They have a great deal of time in which to enforce it.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Guardian's Test

The texts say a vault waits beyond. They warn that worthiness is tested before entry, and no surviving copy explains what worthiness means. The Sable Watch insists the guardian answers to a seal nobody now holds, while a rival party arrives carrying a Hollow Crown's Writ and a very different opinion.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Shifting Sands of Time
entries.flavour: The ruin does not keep time honestly. Glyphs flare and gutter. Soot drifts uphill in the corners. Stone that bore a traveller's weight at dawn may open beneath them by noon. Relics surface when the place remembers them and sink before anyone can make a clean claim, and the Sable Watch will register whatever is carried back to Sablekeep, whether the finder wishes it registered or not.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Sealed Archive
entries.flavour: A sealed archive lies under a fractured basilica in the dead empire's heart: tablets, scrolls, debt records, and sermons the Sable Watch would rather see burned than read. Dust chokes the corridors. Scavengers have gnawed through the newer shelves. Something older keeps the inner stacks in order, and they have waited longer than Sablekeep has stood for someone to disturb them.

entries.title: Scenario 5: The Reliquary of Broken Saints
entries.flavour: Broken statues and smashed reliquaries fill the hall, and sanctified bone and silver remain in the wreckage, too holy to abandon and too valuable to leave. Sablekeep needs the relics to keep its braziers lit and its authority legal, and will pay to register every fragment. The dead here are not confused. They swore to guard these relics, and death has not released them from the oath.

brief.identity: The Reliquary of Broken Saints, an Ashlands hall filled with broken statues and smashed reliquaries, its sanctified bone and silver guarded by dead who swore an oath.

entries.title: Scenario 6: The Iron-Vein Vault
entries.flavour: The vault has been sealed for two generations. Karnessa Iron-Vein pressed their blood into the iron door when something inside began to leak through the walls, and the seal has held. Until now. Tremors along the imperial roads have cracked the outer binding, and something below is pushing. Sablekeep sends one party to reinforce the seal before whatever waits finishes their work; a rival patron sends another to open the vault and price what was sealed there. The vault does not care about either contract.

entries.title: Scenario 1: The Crystal Harvest
entries.flavour: A new cavern has opened beneath the broken mountains, and its crystal veins pulse with cold light and drag iron filings across the floor. Deepwarden's forges would trade a season of grain for a vein this clean. The prospectors who found it have already lied about its location, and both parties arrive before the lie can harden into a map.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Chasm Crossing
entries.flavour: A chasm splits the caverns like a wound in the world, crossed only by narrow ledges in broken pieces. A Survey Map must reach the Lantern Council before Deepwarden's rivals can claim the new diggings. Things cling to the dark stone below the ledges and wait for a hand to shake. The Council wants the map. It does not ask what the things want.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Quake
entries.flavour: The old tunnels shook themselves open before dawn, and gemstone veins glimmer where the support beams snapped. Aftershocks still run through the stone. Deepwarden wants the gems hauled out before the shafts settle, and the usual exits are already blocked. The Dark has noticed the new air, and it is not the only thing moving toward it.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Undermarches Outpost Raid
entries.flavour: Scouts found an outpost below an old road shrine and did not stay to count the banners. Plans for a surface incursion lie inside, and so does the officer who drew them. Deepwarden wants the plans more than it wants the credit, and two parties descend under separate seals, each ordered to take the plans and claim the victory before the other can sell it.

entries.title: Scenario 5: The Shadowed Under Passage
entries.flavour: This passage has been touched by a colder dark than stone can explain. Breath sounds wrong here. The shadows lie against the light instead of with it. A Heart of Shadow waits below, prized by those who bargain with the deep elves and feared by anyone who has read Deepwarden's old warnings. The Lantern Council would rather it stayed lost. Someone with coin disagrees.

entries.title: Scenario 6: The Ritual of Shadow Binding
entries.flavour: In a cavern without honest light, deep elf priests have drawn a binding circle around something that answers from the dark below the Dark. One patron in Deepwarden wants the rite broken before it finishes. Another wants the circle lifted out intact, sigils and all, and will not say for whom. The thing inside the circle has not been consulted.

entries.title: Scenario 1: Plunder of the Frozen Ruins
entries.flavour: The Pale City is littered with magical treasure because its people froze too quickly to hide it, and Hearthhold has lived for generations by thawing out what they left. A promising ruin has cracked open under the snow. Both parties enter before the frozen citizens notice another room has been disturbed, because the citizens do notice, eventually, and they do not forgive trespass.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Alchemist's Frozen Laboratory
entries.flavour: In the ice-locked Silent District, north along the road out of Hearthhold, an alchemist's laboratory remains sealed under frost. The formula inside might be worth a village, and Hearthhold burns through everything it owns just to stay warm. The cold has preserved the benches, the bottles, the last mistakes, and the guardians left to watch them. Some things in that laboratory were never meant to thaw.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Haunted Mausoleum

Their heirlooms remain in the crypt, polished by cold and watched by names too proud to fade. Hearthhold needs whatever can be sold to buy another winter's fuel. The Court does not recognize the sale.

The tinker is dust. The orders remain. Hearthhold's fire-watch wants the intact cores and the notebooks explaining how not to die retrieving them, because a Bastion this poor cannot leave brass that still moves.

Hearthhold needs the gold more than it fears the breath, which is the kind of arithmetic only the poorest Bastion does out loud. The second part of the story has never discouraged the first kind of listener.

Its ruler is the Frost Bailiff Magistrate, who keeps bound spirits and carved servants close and passes sentences that were old before Hearthhold was founded. At the centre of the chamber lies the Heartfrost Shard, cold enough to make breath sound like prayer. Hearthhold wants the Shard. The Magistrate has not adjourned.

Saltspire sells water as sovereignty, and an oasis it does not control is a debt it cannot collect. One contract from the Well-Keepers says liberation. A rival contract says seizure. The water will not ask which seal is righteous.

entries.title: Scenario 1: The Reliquary of Edrava Salttide
entries.flavour: Recent floods opened a grave-house that The Mire had kept sealed for two hundred years. Edrava Salttide, the salt-coast's last great toll-lord, who fed their enemies to the tide and married four pirate-kings in succession, was laid here with a reliquary no Bastion will admit to wanting and every Bastion has quietly sent parties to find. Reedmarch knew where it lay all along and sold the location twice. Both parties enter before the dead gather the strength to close the door again. The water smells of salt. There is no ocean for eighty miles.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Lizardfolk's Stolen Offerings

Another names the silver recoverable property, and Reedmarch will broker either errand for its usual cut of silence.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Mire Titan's Fen
entries.flavour: A Mire Titan has claimed the bubbling fen, and glimmering geodes lie scattered through their territory like bait, because that is more or less what they are. Hunters arrive with hooks, ropes, and prayers. Thieves arrive lighter and usually leave that way. Reedmarch wants the geodes and does not much care which trade brings them in, so long as the fen stays quiet about the rest.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Blighted Heartwood
entries.flavour: Blight has wrapped the swamp growth around a pulsing Heartwood that beats under the bark like a buried organ. One patron wants it destroyed before the rot spreads to the ferry-roads Reedmarch lives on. Another wants its corruption bottled and carried off, and neither wants to be the one holding it on the way home. The Marsh Council would prefer the whole matter stay unspoken.

entries.title: Scenario 5: Salttide's Reckoning
entries.flavour: A curse lies over the sacred island like oil on water. Edrava Salttide has made a ritual of the place, the same ritual they once used to curse the harbours that refused their ships, now turned on the living who entered The Mire without paying the toll. The reeds bend toward the island. The water smells of brine, this far from any sea. Reedmarch sent one party to break the working, and let a rival sell the other a contract whose small print it has not read.

entries.title: Scenario 6: The Serpent's Sunken Hoard
entries.flavour: A flooded sinkhole has opened in the black water, and something ancient coils below it, older than Reedmarch's oldest ferry-family. Their hide, their hoard, and their death would each command a price in a different market. The water is dark enough to hide which one is being hunted, and Reedmarch prefers it that way. Whatever is down there has paid the toll longer than anyone alive, and does not intend to stop now.

entries.title: 11.1 Campaign Overview
entries.flavour: A Stronghold is not a castle in the noble sense. No ancient bloodline sanctifies it. No bard remembers its founding. It is a claim driven into a dying world with coin, fear, salvage, and stubborn labour. Its stones come from ruined shrines, abandoned watch-keeps, broken bridges, and walls that failed other people first. Its gates are paid for with burial gold, bounty coin, chapel debt, and the last wages of the dead.
